title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: Does this release change the schema?
text:
Every upgrade guide and CHANGELOG entry must answer these questions:

| Question | Where to record |
|----------|-----------------|
| New numbered migration(s)? | Highest `NNN_*.sql`; `manifest.toml` `compat_serve_max` |
| Epoch coverage? | Add `[[epoch]]` to `scripts/spec150/epochs.toml` when the tag exists. Until then, pin the working set under `[unreleased]` (hash, max, file count). |
| Operator steps? | Link [upgrading.md](upgrading.md); note if migrate is a no-op |
| Acc re-score needed? | Honest residual in the cut notes |

`scripts/release_gates.sh` fails if checksums drift, if a published tag lacks an epoch, or if the docs claim a schema maximum other than the highest numbered migration.

title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: Gate options
text:
- **Clippy:** `make release-gates` runs workspace clippy. It also runs a slower per-crate clippy loop unless `RELEASE_SKIP_PER_CRATE_CLIPPY=1` is set.
- **Lib tests:** the script runs the workspace lib tests unless `RELEASE_SKIP_LIB_TESTS=1` is set.
- **CI:** the release workflows set both variables, because `ci.yml` already runs the lib suite and per-crate clippy is redundant with workspace clippy.

**OpenAPI / Swagger (required before tag):** regenerate with `make codegen-openapi-refresh`, then run `cargo test -p edgequake-api --test spec027_api_contract`. On a running API, `curl -s http://localhost:8080/api-docs/openapi.json | jq -r '.info.version'` must equal `VERSION`.

**Package dry-run (not a crates.io upload):**

```bash
cd edgequake
for c in edgequake-observability edgequake-storage edgequake-pdf edgequake-pipeline \
         edgequake-query edgequake-tasks edgequake-auth edgequake-audit \
         edgequake-rate-limiter edgequake-core edgequake-api; do
  cargo package -p "$c" --allow-dirty --no-verify 2>/dev/null || cargo package -p "$c" --list >/dev/null
done
```

title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: 2) CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
text:
- `CI` (fmt, clippy, nextest lib, docs, build) must be green.
- `Test Quality Gates` (invariants, test-count floor, e2e lint and UI) must be green.
- `Release Gates` must be green, or the tag push runs the same preflight inside `release-docker.yml`.
- `SPEC-046 ACC` must be green when query, storage, or spec paths change.
- `SPEC-013 PR Proof` and the PostgreSQL integration tests must be green when those paths change.
- `Migration Guard` Layer 4 must be green before a schema cut. It runs `e2e_spec164_v034_large_upgrade`: a real v0.34.0 database (schema 169, the published checksum of migration 167) with 80,000 documents, upgraded by `edgequake migrate` through 202. Raw `sqlx migrate run` in Layer 2 does not fold a split ledger or repair that checksum.
- Ignore unrelated external automation failures (for example Dependabot noise) only when all required project gates are green.

**Speed knobs:** a shared Swatinem cache (`shared-key: edgequake-ci`), sparse crates.io index, no incremental builds, `--locked`, cancel-in-progress, and no duplicate workspace lib compile across Quality Gates and Release Gates.

**Docker CD anti-flake gates** (run by `make release-gates` and `scripts/release_gates.sh`):

- `scripts/check_docker_api_context.sh`: Cargo `[[bench]]` and `[[example]]` paths must exist, the Dockerfile must `COPY` them, and `.dockerignore` must not exclude them.
- `next.config.ts` size-limit guard: `proxyClientMaxBodySize` must be numeric (`DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`).
- The README badge version must match `VERSION`, Cargo, and `package.json`.
- Per-crate package versions must be `version.workspace = true` or equal `VERSION`.
- `edgequake_webui/openapi/openapi.snapshot.json` `info.version` must equal `VERSION`.

title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: 3) Cut the Release
text:
Push the version tag after the local gates pass:

```bash
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

The tag triggers two workflows:

- `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` builds multi-arch API, frontend, and triple-track Postgres images. It pushes `:VERSION` and `:latest` tags, plus `:VERSION-pg16`, `:VERSION-pg17`, and `:VERSION-pg18`, to GHCR. It creates or updates the GitHub Release notes for the tag.
- `.github/workflows/release-keycloak.yml` builds the Keycloak image after smoke-testing it with `scripts/keycloak_smoke.py`.

Both `linux/amd64` (ubuntu-latest) and `linux/arm64` (native ARM64 runner, no QEMU) are built in parallel and merged into one multi-arch manifest. The same tag works on x86 servers, Apple Silicon Macs, and AWS Graviton instances.

**Manual run and republish:**

- To run the Docker workflow without a new tag, use **Actions → Release — Docker (GHCR) → Run workflow** and enter `tag_name`.
- To republish after a CD fix on a release branch, run `gh workflow run "Release — Docker (GHCR)" --ref release/vX.Y.Z -f tag_name=vX.Y.Z`. The workflow builds from the branch and still publishes the `X.Y.Z` and `latest` tags.

**Do not use `make version-tag`.** It commits, tags, and pushes in one step, so it skips the review of the local gates. Use the explicit `git tag` and `git push` commands above.

text:
**Mandatory local gate** before tagging a product cut. Dual-SUT GraphRAG-Bench Acc (EdgeQuake `mix` vs LightRAG `mix`, medical-mid **n=200**) is **not** part of `make release-gates` or GitHub Actions. It needs Mistral keys, Postgres, LightRAG, and roughly 1 to 3 hours or more of wall time. It is the same class as the SPEC-042 battle tests: required at cut time, not in CI.

**Not substitutes:** `make spec046-acc` (deterministic Hybrid ACC, no LightRAG) · `make bench001-smoke-acc` (n=40 daily only; **not** the release Acc score) · an "EQ beats LightRAG" claim (the promote checklist stops it unless CI excludes 0).

title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: Upgrade notes: SPEC-091 (v0.22.0 to v0.23.0)
text:
Published **v0.22.0** stops at migration **105**. **v0.23.0** adds migrations **106–141**, including irreversible drops (`125` KV, `126` chunk-vector, `131` fleet-vector). Do **not** treat a routine image bump as safe until the soak gate is green.

- Short guide: [migrate-to-0.23.md](./migrate-to-0.23.md)
- Operator runbook: [spec091-upgrade-from-v0.22.0.md](./spec091-upgrade-from-v0.22.0.md)
- Automated multi-tenant soak: `make spec93-migration-assessment` (PG16, 17, and 18 realism; see [`specs/93-migration-assessment/`](../../specs/93-migration-assessment/)). Smoke: `make spec091-upgrade-soak`.
- Spec status: [`specs/091-simplify-data-layer/README.md`](../../specs/091-simplify-data-layer/README.md)
- **Boot migration gating (LD-15, behavior change):** images built from HEAD never auto-migrate at container start. Boot exits **78** with a dry-run or migrate hint when the schema is behind or newer. Release notes must call this out. Deploys need a one-shot migrate step (a Compose service or a Kubernetes Job; examples are in the runbook) before new replicas can start. Spec: [`specs/091-simplify-data-layer/17-boot-migration-gating.md`](../../specs/091-simplify-data-layer/17-boot-migration-gating.md)

title: Release & CD Cycle
heading: Lessons from past cuts
text:
- **OpenAPI refresh is mandatory** after `version-bump`. `openapi.snapshot.json` `info.version` must equal `VERSION`, or the release gates fail.
- **The workspace is not crates.io.** Bump all members together, dry-run `cargo package`, and ship through the GHCR tag only.
- **Do not use `make version-tag`.** It pushes automatically. Tag explicitly after the local gates pass.
- **Frontend CD** builds [`edgequake_webui/Dockerfile`](../../edgequake_webui/Dockerfile), not `edgequake/docker/Dockerfile.frontend`. It must `COPY openapi/`, and it should prefer relative imports for `schema.d.ts`, because `@/*` shadows `@/openapi/*`.
- **Vision timeouts (X-30):** vision stall messages must carry `Operation timed out` and `failure_class=`. `from_processing_error` must use the timeout factory, or the progress-aware breaker never trips.
- **Benchmark artifacts:** keep scorecards only. The medical-full raw JSON exceeds GitHub's 100 MB limit, so gitignore `artifacts/medical-full*` and `history/medical-full-*`. Smoke artifacts may be committed for reproducibility, but cite publish-pack pointers for Acc claims.
- **Acc language:** cite a statistical tie (about 1.01× on a fair cold run). Do not claim an Acc win. The warm LightRAG speed advantage was cache, not algorithm (see [063](../../specs/001-benchmark/001-edgquake-improvements/063-why-lightrag-faster-cache-fairness.md)).
- **Baseline flakes:** AGE neighbor tests and the SPEC-013 AGE `LOAD` check can stay red when triaged as baseline. Never merge past SPEC-006, clippy, workspace lib, or release-gates failures.
- **Soft labels:** clean opaque AGE node IDs still need a re-ingest.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Runtime config and authentication hardening
text: This page is for operators who run EdgeQuake on a shared or public network. It covers what the API refuses to start with, the settings to use in production, and how to create the first user. To turn login on for the first time, start with [Enable login](auth-quickstart.md). SSO providers (Keycloak, Entra, Google, GitHub) are covered in [Security: authentication](../security/authentication/index.md).

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: What the API checks at startup
text:
The API validates its security settings before it opens a port. A fatal check stops the process with exit code 1. A warning is logged and startup continues, unless `EDGEQUAKE_STRICT_STARTUP=1` turns every warning into a fatal error.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
flowchart TD
  A["API starts"] --> B{"JWT_SECRET strong?"}
  B -->|No, dev mode off| X1["Exit 1"]
  B -->|Yes, or dev mode on| C{"Auth off on remote DB, dev mode off?"}
  C -->|Yes| X2["Exit 1"]
  C -->|No| D{"Remote DB, dev mode off, no CORS list?"}
  D -->|Yes| X3["Exit 1"]
  D -->|No| E{"Any warnings and STRICT_STARTUP=1?"}
  E -->|Yes| X4["Exit 1"]
  E -->|No| F["Serve"]
%% eq-classes
classDef eqStore fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#10B981,color:#064E3B
class C,D eqStore
```

The checks run top to bottom, and the first failing check stops startup. Warnings only matter when strict startup is on.

A **remote DB** is a `DATABASE_URL` whose host is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or `host.docker.internal`. The Compose service host `postgres` therefore counts as remote.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: What the API checks at startup
text:
| Check | Fatal when | Warning when |
|-------|-----------|--------------|
| `JWT_SECRET` | It is the shipped default or shorter than 32 bytes, and dev mode is off. | The same, with dev mode on. |
| Auth off on a remote database | Auth off, dev mode off, remote `DATABASE_URL`. | n/a |
| CORS | `EDGEQUAKE_CORS_ORIGINS` is empty, dev mode off, remote `DATABASE_URL`. | n/a |
| Credentials | n/a | Auth on but no `EDGEQUAKE_API_KEYS` or `EDGEQUAKE_MASTER_API_KEY`. |
| Open registration | n/a | `ALLOW_REGISTRATION` is true (the default) with auth on and dev mode off. |
| Rate limit | n/a | `EDGEQUAKE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` is off and dev mode off. |
| Secrets key | n/a | `EDGEQUAKE_SECRETS_KEY` is unset and dev mode off. Connection API keys cannot be saved. |

Set `EDGEQUAKE_STRICT_STARTUP=1` in production once the warnings are clean.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Recommended production settings
text:
```bash
export EDGEQUAKE_AUTH_ENABLED=true
export EDGEQUAKE_DEV_MODE=false                    # or leave unset
export JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"        # 32 bytes or more
export EDGEQUAKE_CORS_ORIGINS="https://app.example.com"
export EDGEQUAKE_MASTER_API_KEY="replace-with-a-strong-secret"
export ALLOW_REGISTRATION=false
export EDGEQUAKE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true
export EDGEQUAKE_SECRETS_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"   # see Providers > Security
export EDGEQUAKE_STRICT_STARTUP=1

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Web UI
text:
export NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED=true
export NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_DEMO_LOGIN=true
```

The web UI reads `EDGEQUAKE_API_URL` at request time. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are baked into the image at build time, so prefer the runtime variable for the API URL.

Access tokens last 15 minutes by default (`JWT_EXPIRY_SECONDS`), and refresh tokens last 30 days (`REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS`). Five failed logins (`MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS`) lock an account for 15 minutes (`LOCKOUT_DURATION_MINUTES`).

For the full list of variables, see [Configuration](configuration.md). For key format and storage of provider secrets, see [Provider security](../providers/security.md).

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Local development (open API)
text:
`make dev` sets `EDGEQUAKE_DEV_MODE=true` when `DEV_AUTH_ENABLED=false`, which is the default. The [Docker quickstart](docker-quickstart.md) does the same for container demos. Do not use open mode on a shared network.

```bash
export EDGEQUAKE_DEV_MODE=true   # explicit local open API
```

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Auth precedence
text:
When several settings disagree, the API resolves them in this order:

1. `EDGEQUAKE_AUTH_ENABLED`, or its alias `AUTH_ENABLED`, when set.
2. `EDGEQUAKE_AUTH_DISABLED=true`.
3. `EDGEQUAKE_DEV_MODE=true` (auth off).
4. Default: auth on.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Bootstrap an admin user
text:
The API creates one admin on startup when auth is on, dev mode is off, and no login-capable user exists. Set the credentials before the first start:

```bash
export EDGEQUAKE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin          # default: admin
export EDGEQUAKE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD='a-long-unique-password'
export EDGEQUAKE_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com # default: <username>@localhost
```

If the password is not set and no login-capable user exists, the API logs a warning and nobody can sign in. If a user with the bootstrap name exists but has no usable password hash, the bootstrap upgrades it to an admin. Upgrades from before v0.15 also import old `auth:user:*` identity rows into PostgreSQL.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Create a user with the master key
text:
Use this when dev mode is on, or to add users later:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $EDGEQUAKE_MASTER_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "username": "admin",
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "a-long-unique-password",
    "role": "admin"
  }'
```

The `role` field is optional and defaults to `user`. Passwords must be 8 to 128 characters. Send the key as `X-API-Key: <key>` or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Expected behavior
text:
| State | What users see |
|-------|----------------|
| Auth off | Dashboard loads without login. Demo flows work. |
| Auth on | Dashboard routes redirect to the login page. The demo login is hidden when `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_DEMO_LOGIN=true`. Protected endpoints need a JWT or API key. |

Anonymous chat is a separate switch. `EDGEQUAKE_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS` (default `true`) lets unauthenticated users share a guest user for chat. Set it to `false` to return 401 or 403 instead.

title: Runtime config and authentication hardening
heading: Troubleshooting
text: See the table in [Enable login](auth-quickstart.md#troubleshooting). To see what the API decided at boot, run `edgequake doctor`. The `security_posture` block of `GET /health` shows the same signals at runtime (see [Monitoring](monitoring.md)).

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
text:
This runbook is for operators who upgrade a live Postgres database from GHCR **v0.22.0** (migrations up to **105**, KV as the source of truth) to **v0.23.0 or later** (migrations **106–142**: the typed relational source of truth, irreversible KV and vector drops, the RM0–RM5 outbox drain, citation and chunk FTS, AGE citation indexes, SPEC-098 spine and lifecycle, and the **SPEC-105** legacy cutover assert).

For the short version, read [Migrate to v0.23.0](./migrate-to-0.23.md). The spec pack is in [`specs/091-simplify-data-layer/`](../../specs/091-simplify-data-layer/). Risks R-21 to R-29 are in `09-risk-register.md`.

> **Automated proof:** `make spec93-migration-assessment` (PG16, 17 and 18 realism), `make spec091-upgrade-soak` (smoke) and `make spec091-gates`. The formal pack is in [`specs/93-migration-assessment/`](../../specs/93-migration-assessment/).

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Risk summary
text:
| Risk | Why it matters | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Migration **125** is irreversible | After the `eq_*_kv` drop, rollback means **restoring from backup** | The `--confirm-drop` gate; a durable-row guard aborts if the typed source of truth is incomplete |
| Replica skew (R-27) | A stale binary treats missing KV as a hard error and fails ingests | Roll **all** replicas to the write-stop build before or with the drop |
| Stale `kv` or `dual` flags | After the drop, these flags hit `42P01` or take the wrong path | Keep `EDGEQUAKE_CHUNK_TEXT_AUTHORITY` and `EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_*=relational`; check with `edgequake migrate console` |
| Serving fence (R-28) | A wrong JOIN zeroes retrieval for every workspace | Keep the fence on after a query proof; the JOIN must use `public.chunk_serving_state` |
| Multi-tenant shell drift (R-21, R-24) | A wipe or membership change can miss shell documents | Schema-qualify `public.documents`; check that a wipe in one workspace leaves the others intact |

**Verdict:** treat this upgrade as **high operational risk** until `make spec93-migration-assessment` is green for your class of data, or until an equivalent restore of a production dump passes.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Prerequisites
text:
1. A verified backup or restore point. A custom-format `pg_dump -Fc` is recommended.
2. pgvector 0.8.2 or later (0.8.5 preferred), and AGE at the tier pinned for your Postgres major.
3. Every replica runs the **same** v0.23.0 write-stop binary. Mixed fleets are not allowed across the drop.
4. A maintenance window long enough for the SQL backfills 117–124, plus the optional chunk-text job on large corpora.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Flag matrix
text:
Serving boot **never** applies migrations. A pending schema makes the server exit 78 with a dry-run hint. `edgequake migrate` is the only schema writer.

```bash
export EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATION_MODE=automatic      # or verify, then automatic
export EDGEQUAKE_CHUNK_TEXT_AUTHORITY=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_DOC_HASH=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_WSDOC=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_CHECKPOINT=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_ARTIFACT=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_INJECTION=relational
export EDGEQUAKE_KV_FAMILY_METADATA=relational

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Do NOT set EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATION_CONFIRM_DROP=1 in a shared env file.
text:
```

`make dev` defaults assume a **post-drop** database. Do not copy them onto a mid-upgrade v0.22.0 fleet without reading this runbook.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Operator sequence
text:
```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
flowchart TB
    A["Fleet on v0.22.0 (schema up to 105)"] --> B["Back up Postgres (pg_dump -Fc)"]
    B --> C["Roll ALL replicas to the 0.23.0 write-stop build"]
    C --> D["migrate dry-run (preview, no writes)"]
    D --> E["migrate (expandable steps first; stops before the drops)"]
    E --> F["migrate --confirm-drop (irreversible 125, 126, 131)"]
    F --> G["Start the 0.23.0 API (verify-only boot)"]
    G --> H["Verify tenants, wipe, assets, and query"]
    H --> I["Turn the serving fence on"]
%% eq-classes
classDef eqStore fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#10B981,color:#064E3B
class B eqStore
```

Read the diagram top to bottom; the numbered steps below expand each box.

0. **Dry run** (preview only). Point `DATABASE_URL` at the target database and inspect the pending work. Nothing is applied.

   ```bash
   cargo run -p edgequake --features postgres -- migrate dry-run
   ```

   The run ends with `dry-run complete: no migrations applied (preview only).` It lists each pending migration and marks 125 as irreversible. Check the drop readiness it reports before you continue.

1. **Back up** the database (`pg_dump -Fc` or a volume snapshot) and record the restore point.
2. **Drain or stop writers** if your SLO needs a quiet window. This is recommended before `--confirm-drop`.
3. **Roll every API replica** to the v0.23.0 binary that treats KV `42P01` as "source gone" (write-stop). Do not leave a v0.22.0 API process attached after 125.
4. Run the expandable migrations, then check the guards:

   ```bash
   cargo run -p edgequake --features postgres -- migrate
   cargo run -p edgequake --features postgres -- migrate console
   cargo run -p edgequake --features postgres -- migrate guard
   ```

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Operator sequence
text:
The expandable steps run first. When only irreversible drops remain, the command exits 0 with a WARN. If an irreversible drop blocks a later expandable migration, the command refuses to run.

5. When you are ready to contract (irreversible):

   ```bash
   cargo run -p edgequake --features postgres -- migrate --confirm-drop
   ```

   sqlx applies the pending migrations 106–125 in order. The family SQL backfills (117–124) run first. Migration **125** then purges the KV keys that already exist in the typed source of truth, and runs the durable-row guard. If un-migrated residue remains, 125 aborts and the database stays pre-drop. Fix the residue, restore if needed, and retry. On success, stdout reports `KV store dropped (migration 125). Rollback = restore from backup.`

6. **Start the v0.23.0 API** with the relational flag matrix above. Boot only verifies the schema. If any migration were still pending, the server would exit 78.
7. **Verify** for each tenant and workspace:
   - `GET /health` reports healthy.
   - The document list is non-empty where documents were seeded.
   - Queries return grounded sources, not `sources: null` with populated vectors.
   - Asset paths do not return 500 with `relation eq_*_kv does not exist`.
   - A wipe in one workspace leaves the other workspaces and tenants intact.
8. Optionally set `EDGEQUAKE_SERVING_FENCE=on` after a successful query proof.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Boot gate (LD-15)
text:
Server start never applies versioned schema. Boot reads `_sqlx_migrations` and decides:

- **Expandable migrations pending:** exit **78** (`EX_CONFIG`), with the pending count and the `migrate dry-run` and `migrate` hints.
- **Only irreversible drops pending (125, 126, 131):** boot continues with a WARN. Health still reports `migration_required` until `--confirm-drop` runs (LD-07).
- **Database newer than the binary:** exit 78 (downgrade protection).
- **Up to date:** the server serves. Reconcile hooks stay read-only probes.

`/health.schema.pending_count` and `migration_required` show drift after boot, for example when a replica is still up while the fleet migrated. Spec: [`specs/091-simplify-data-layer/17-boot-migration-gating.md`](../../specs/091-simplify-data-layer/17-boot-migration-gating.md).

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Docker Compose: one-shot migrate service
text:
```yaml
services:
  migrate:
    image: ghcr.io/raphaelmansuy/edgequake:${EDGEQUAKE_VERSION}
    command: ["migrate"]              # add "dry-run" for a preview-only run
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://edgequake:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/edgequake
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }
    restart: "no"                     # one-shot; exits 0 when the schema is current

  api:
    image: ghcr.io/raphaelmansuy/edgequake:${EDGEQUAKE_VERSION}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
```

Migrations 125 and 126 on an **upgraded** database still need an explicit one-shot with `command: ["migrate", "--confirm-drop"]`, run after you review the `dry-run`. Never put that in an always-on service. A fresh install (no applied migrations) needs no flag.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Kubernetes: migrate Job before the Deployment rolls
text:
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: edgequake-migrate }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: ghcr.io/raphaelmansuy/edgequake:VERSION
          args: ["migrate"]           # or ["migrate", "--confirm-drop"] after a dry-run review
          env:
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: edgequake-db, key: url } }
```

Apply the Job, wait for it to complete, then roll the Deployment. New replicas crash-loop with exit 78 until the Job completes, which makes the wait visible. For defence in depth, you can also gate readiness on `/health.schema.migration_required == false`.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Rollback
text:
| Phase | Rollback |
| --- | --- |
| Before `--confirm-drop` completes 125 | Redeploy the previous binary. Additive (expand-phase) migrations may remain. |
| After 125 is applied | **Restore from backup only.** There is no flag flip that brings back the dropped `eq_*_kv` tables. |

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
flowchart TB
    A{"Has migration 125 been applied?"} -->|no| B["Redeploy the previous API image"]
    B --> C["Additive migrations may remain; that is safe"]
    A -->|yes| D["Restore the pre-upgrade backup"]
    D --> E["No flag can undo the KV drop"]
%% eq-classes
classDef eqStore fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#10B981,color:#064E3B
class A,C,E eqStore
```

Notice that the rollback path depends on whether migration 125 has already dropped the KV tables.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Legacy smoke test (tiny corpus, default postgres tag)
text:
make spec091-upgrade-soak
```

**SPEC-93** is the binding proof pack, in [`specs/93-migration-assessment/`](../../specs/93-migration-assessment/). It pulls `ghcr.io/raphaelmansuy/edgequake:0.22.0` and the matching `edgequake-postgres:0.22.0-pg{16,17,18}` images. It seeds a realism corpus, dumps the database, runs the v0.23.0 `migrate dry-run` (asserting a preview and no schema advance), then runs `migrate --confirm-drop` through migrations **106–141**. Finally it asserts isolation, listing, wipe, assets, and retrieval with the fence on. Reports are in `specs/93-migration-assessment/reports/`.

title: SPEC-091 — Upgrade from v0.22.0
heading: Manual soak with a real dump
text:
1. Restore a v0.22.0-era dump into an ephemeral Postgres of the same major version.
2. Point `DATABASE_URL` at it and follow the operator sequence above.
3. Run the same HTTP and SQL checks as the soak script (multi-tenant isolation and wipe).

Rehearse on a staging restore before you run `--confirm-drop` in production.

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
text: Typed fleet embeddings need relational spine rows. Migrations **139** (entities), **140** (EDGE arbiter and relationships) and **141** (document lifecycle statuses) fix the spine and the edge index. Run them on PostgreSQL **16, 17 or 18**. Use this page when reprocess or delete fails with the errors listed below.

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: Migration chain
text:
```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
flowchart LR
    A["139: ensure entities for the typed fleet foreign key"] --> B["140: one EDGE arbiter and the relationships spine"]
    B --> C["141: documents accept deleting and delete_failed"]
    A -.-> P1["progress: spec098_spine_ensure_progress"]
    B -.-> P2["progress: spec098_edge_arbiter_progress"]
%% eq-classes
classDef eqBad fill:#FEE2E2,stroke:#EF4444,color:#7F1D1D
class C eqBad
```

Each migration adds one piece of the spine. Migrations 139 and 140 also have manual `apply.sql` scripts in `edgequake/migrations/support/`, which the re-run steps below use.

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: Hot path
text:
1. A saturated `SOURCE_IDS` KEEP still upserts the relational spine. The AGE description mutation is skipped. Reprocess should not fail with `typed fleet mirror resolved 0/N`.
2. Native AGE edge upserts use a **single** arbiter, `idx_edge_eq_source_target_rel (eq_source_id, eq_target_id, eq_rel_type)`. A reprocess of a multi-chunk extract must not fail with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time`.
3. With `EDGEQUAKE_NATIVE_GRAPH_WRITES=0` (debug mode), Cypher `MERGE` also keys edges on `(source_id, target_id, relation_type)`. The multigraph semantics stay the same.
4. **Near-complete mirror misses (`999/1000`).** If the SPEC-098 miss samples look like `NAME_WITH_->_ARROW->OTHER:REL`, the cause is usually the legacy-key parse, not a missing spine. Entity names that contain `->` break it. The parser first tries index-guided splits (SPEC-133: both endpoints must resolve in `entities`). It then falls back to the last `->` (`parse_relationship_legacy_key`). Reprocess after the upgrade. Do not re-run 139 or 140 only for this error. Pathological names with several resolvable splits or a `:` remain a known limit (SPEC-133 LAW-133-9).

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: EDGE index checklist
text:
```sql
-- Replace 'edgequake' with your graph name (server_config.age_graph_name).
SELECT indexname
FROM pg_indexes
WHERE schemaname = 'edgequake' AND tablename = 'EDGE'
ORDER BY 1;
```

| Index | Required |
|-------|----------|
| `idx_edge_eq_source_target_rel` | **Yes** (the 3-column multigraph arbiter) |
| `idx_edge_eq_source_target` | **No**; must be dropped |
| `idx_edge_source_target_unique` | **No**; must be dropped |

The runtime bootstrap (`ensure_eq_id_columns` and `reconcile_legacy_graph_arbiters`) also drops legacy UNIQUE constraints, even when the schema already looks ready.

heading: Migration reference

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: Document delete lifecycle
text:
Notice that a failed cascade parks the document in `delete_failed` until you retry the delete.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> deleting: delete admitted
    deleting --> removed: cascade succeeds
    deleting --> delete_failed: cascade fails
    delete_failed --> deleting: retry Delete
    removed --> [*]
```

Both projections must agree during the delete (LAW-098-9). Check the SQL side, then the KV side:

```sql
-- Both projections must agree (LAW-098-9)
SELECT id, status FROM documents WHERE status IN ('deleting', 'delete_failed');
```

The KV `*-metadata` entry for the same ID must also show `"status":"deleting"`. After a successful delete, the ID must be absent from SQL `documents`, from KV `*-metadata`, and from `GET /documents`.

Apply migration 141 before you rely on these statuses:

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f edgequake/migrations/support/141/apply.sql
```

title: SPEC-098 — Entity spine and EDGE arbiter (operator)
heading: Delete failure messages
text:
- **`event=spec098_sql_deleting_mirror_failed` in the admit log.** The SQL `CHECK` still rejects `deleting` and `delete_failed` (before migration 141). KV admit still succeeds and the delete task runs. Re-apply `support/141` so the list dual-write can mirror the lifecycle statuses.
- **`Post-proof failed: N nodes and M edges still reference document sources`.** Deploy the cascade Replace write-mode fix, then **retry Delete** on the `delete_failed` rows. Shared-entity pruning must persist without `eq_merge_graph_properties` re-adding the pruned `source_ids`.
- Failed cascades leave `status=delete_failed`, not the pipeline `failed` status. Batch task results list each failed document with a reason, for root-cause analysis.

4. If you see checksum drift on 125 or 131 (or on 118 or 121 after the SPEC-110 body repair), repair once and unset the variable:

   ```bash

5. If the cutover is still running, run the engine jobs: `w3-chunk-embedding-backfill`, `iw2-fleet-embedding-backfill`, `iw2-fleet-provenance-stamp`.
6. When the guard is ready, run `edgequake migrate --confirm-drop`.

text:
> **From:** v0.24.2 · **To:** v0.24.3 · **CD:** GHCR (`edgequake`, `edgequake-frontend`, `edgequake-postgres`)

This is an operations patch. It hardens the PostgreSQL connection pools (SPEC-112) and makes UTF-8 truncation safe. Use it if your EdgeQuake instances share a PostgreSQL server with other applications. It adds no migrations, so the schema does not change.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.24.3
heading: Sequence
text:
1. Take a backup. This is optional for this patch because there is no schema change.
2. Deploy the v0.24.3 API (and the frontend if you pin it).
3. On a shared PostgreSQL server, set the pool sizes before the restart:

   ```bash
   export EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_SIZE_QUERY=8
   export EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_SIZE_INGEST=6
   export EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_SIZE_QUEUE=2
   export EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_SIZE_ADMIN=1
   export EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_INSTANCE_COUNT=<replicas including rollout overlap>
   # optional: EDGEQUAKE_DB_POOL_BUDGET_MODE=fail
   ```

4. Stop the old instances with SIGTERM, not SIGKILL. SIGTERM drains requests and closes the pools. SIGKILL skips the close.
5. Verify the attribution and the health output (see below).

The pool variables and their defaults are listed in [configuration.md](configuration.md) under **Database**. The detailed ops guide is [`specs/112-connection-pool/07-ops-runbook.md`](../../specs/112-connection-pool/07-ops-runbook.md).

SELECT application_name, state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' GROUP BY 1, 2;

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.26.0
heading: Leftover SPEC-091 DROP OLD (125, 126, 131)
text:
Serving on 0.25 with pending KV or vector drops is **allowed**. Those migrations are not part of the 149 train. If `dry-run` or preflight still lists 125, 126 or 131, you are in the mid-cutover ladder. Follow the flow below. The steps reference [spec091-upgrade-from-v0.22.0.md](spec091-upgrade-from-v0.22.0.md) and [upgrade-to-0.24.2.md](upgrade-to-0.24.2.md) (engine jobs and a GREEN guard). Run the confirm step with a **v0.26.1+** binary ([upgrade-to-0.26.1.md](upgrade-to-0.26.1.md)).

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
flowchart TB
  A["Run migrate dry-run"] --> B{"125, 126 or 131 still pending?"}
  B -->|No| C["Nothing to drop. Finish"]
  B -->|Yes| D["Let the engine jobs finish (upgrade-to-0.24.2)"]
  D --> E{"migrate guard GREEN?"}
  E -->|No| D
  E -->|Yes| F["Take a backup, then migrate --confirm-drop with a 0.26.1+ binary"]
  F --> G["Run migrate again to clear the 142 assert"]
```

The guard must be green before any drop. SQL that finds uncovered rows aborts on purpose. Do not skip the guards. Details are in [`specs/137-issue-migration-25-to-26/09-ops-runbook.md`](../../specs/137-issue-migration-25-to-26/09-ops-runbook.md).

Unknown apply flags fail closed (for example `--confirm-drp`). Do **not** set `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATION_CONFIRM_DROP=1` in a shared env file.

This is an observability patch. Langfuse generation spans now record the full LLM prompt and completion, with no length cut by default. Secrets stay redacted, and ingested document content stays in preview. It adds no migrations, so the schema train stays at **149** from [upgrade-to-0.26.0.md](upgrade-to-0.26.0.md). This minor release ships SPEC-149 (provider access and projection authority) and SPEC-150 (a reliable migration lifecycle). The schema moves from 149 to 159. The API no longer applies migrations at boot, so run `edgequake migrate` before `/ready` returns 200.

| Schema gate | `EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE=wait\|fail`. The code default is **fail**; the Compose file sets **wait** |

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.27.0
heading: Migrate before serve
text:
The schema gate decides at boot whether the API serves, waits, or exits.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Check: API boots
    Check --> Serve: ledger current
    Check --> Wait: pending migrations and mode wait
    Check --> Refuse: pending migrations and mode fail
    Wait --> Check: poll every EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE_POLL seconds
    Refuse --> [*]: exit 78
```

The gate reads the ledger; it never runs DDL. Run migrate first, then start the API.

text:

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
heading: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
text:
> **From:** v0.34.0 (schema **169**) · **To:** v0.35.0 (schema **206**)

**demo.edgequake.com:** this cut installs the 0.35.0 API and WebUI. Non-interactive
migrate leaves Apache AGE installed (migration 171 stays pending). Password auth
remains the demo default.

Fresh install on Postgres without AGE:
[specs/164-pure-postgres-study/README.md](../../specs/164-pure-postgres-study/README.md).

The train is migrations **170** through **206**:

| Migration | What it does | Consent |
|-----------|--------------|---------|
| 170 | Plain graph tables. Does not raise the serving floor, so a v0.34 binary can still serve. | `edgequake migrate` |
| 171 | Drops Apache AGE after the cutover ledger is `ready`. Default is to leave AGE. | `edgequake migrate --drop-age` (or answer yes) |
| 172–202 | Request-path indexes. Do not raise the serving floor. | `edgequake migrate` (applied even when 171 is still pending) |
| 203 | Stored `chunks.legacy_chunk_key` so id lookup is an index condition under row security. | `edgequake migrate` |
| 204 | Label search runs as the table owner so `LIKE` can use the trigram index under row security. | `edgequake migrate` |
| 205 | Drops the empty `ag_catalog` schema left behind after Apache AGE is gone. Refuses if the cutover is not ready or a leftover table has rows. | `edgequake migrate` |
| 206 | Stored `modality` and `current_stage` columns, plus owner-side node search, so those predicates are index conditions under row security. | `edgequake migrate` |

`release_for_schema` maps 170–206 to v0.35.0. Migration **207** ships in [v0.35.1](upgrade-to-0.35.1.md). Schema 169 stays the published v0.33.0 / v0.34.0 point.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
heading: What was proved
text:
Migration-guard CI Layer 4 runs `e2e_spec164_v034_large_upgrade` on PostgreSQL. The test builds a database the way v0.34.0 left it: stop at migration **169**, then rewrite the stored checksum of migration **167** to the hash published in tag `v0.34.0`. It loads 80,000 documents, 40,000 chunks, 30,000 conversations, and 80,000 tasks, then upgrades with the product migrator.

Measured on that corpus ([v034_large_upgrade.json](../../specs/164-pure-postgres-study/measurements/v034_large_upgrade.json)):

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Empty database, migrations 1–169 | 2.008 s |
| Upgrade 170–202 | 3.003 s |
| Row counts | unchanged |
| Ledger | `public._sqlx_migrations` only, head 202 |
| Apache AGE | left installed unless migrate is answered yes (`--drop-age`) |
| `status=failed` page | 0.081 ms, no sequential scan |

The same test folds a stray ledger: if versions 15 and 16 were recorded outside `public`, the next `edgequake migrate` copies them back and drops the stray table.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
heading: Operator steps (when the tag exists)
text:
Until then, use these steps on a backup of a v0.34.0 database if you are rehearsing the train. Full command reference: [upgrading.md](upgrading.md).

```bash
pg_dump -Fc "$DATABASE_URL" > edgequake-$(date +%F).dump
edgequake migrate check
edgequake migrate dry-run
edgequake migrate

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
heading: 171 stays pending until the cutover ledger is ready and you consent:
text:
edgequake migrate --confirm-drop
edgequake migrate status
```

`edgequake migrate status` prints the schema before any data-engine jobs:

```text
schema:
  database : 169 (≈ v0.33.0)
  binary   : 206 (≈ v0.35.0)
  pending  : 36
  drop old : 171 (drops Apache AGE after the SPEC-164 plain-graph ledger is ready)
```

After a successful apply the closing line is `migrate ok: pending_before=… latest=206 applied_this_run=…`. An empty database prints `latest=none`. Lists of versions are spans (`172–206`), and drop steps name what they delete.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.0
heading: What this command will not do
text:
- It will not apply schema from the API process. Only `edgequake migrate` writes numbered migrations.
- It will not drop Apache AGE unless you answer yes. `--confirm-drop` still gates the other DROP OLD steps. Without `--drop-age`, safe schema on both sides of 171 is applied and 171 stays pending.
- It will not repair an unknown checksum. The published v0.34.0 hash of migration 167 is a known fossil and is rewritten to the current file hash before sqlx runs. Any other mismatch stops.
- It will not write a second `_sqlx_migrations` table. Each step pins `search_path` to `public`.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.1
heading: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.1
text:
> **From:** v0.35.0 (schema **206**) · **To:** v0.35.1 (schema **207**)

v0.35.0 already shipped the plain-graph train through migration **206**. This patch adds migration **207** and three runtime fixes. From v0.34.0, apply [upgrade-to-0.35.0.md](upgrade-to-0.35.0.md) first, then this page. `edgequake migrate` on 0.35.1 applies 207 with the rest of the safe schema. It still does not drop Apache AGE unless you pass `--drop-age`.

| Migration | What it does | Consent |
|-----------|--------------|---------|
| 207 | Document lineage lookup runs as the bypass owner so the tenant role can use the lineage indexes under forced AGE row security. | `edgequake migrate` |

`release_for_schema` maps 170–206 to v0.35.0 and 207 to v0.35.1.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.1
heading: What else changed
text:
- After migrate marks `eq_graph_cutover` ready, graph reads and writes stay on `eq_graph_nodes` and `eq_graph_edges`. `EDGEQUAKE_GRAPH_READ=age` has no effect in that state: it does not create AGE label tables and it does not route graph IO back to Apache AGE. Before the ledger is `ready`, the in-progress upgrade path is unchanged.
- Credentialed browser clients on another origin receive their own `Origin` echoed back, with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. The API does not send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
- `GET /api/v1/lineage/documents/{id}` uses the migration 207 lookup instead of scanning every node in the tenant.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.4
heading: What changed
text:
- **#493.** After the ledger is `ready`, deleting a document removes that document's citations from `eq_graph_edges`. A relationship that other documents still cite stays. Singular `source_document_id` and `source_chunk_id` are found, and a citation the projection manifest missed is cleaned by the existing cascade.
- **#494.** `edgequake migrate` can finish the plain-graph cutover when the database role has `statement_timeout` of 10s. The copy is not left with `eq_graph_cutover.status = 'backfilling'` because of that timeout. A timeout that is set for the cutover itself still cancels the copy and rolls it back.
- Gold answers include every supporting clause from the retrieved context.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.5
heading: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.5
text:
> **From:** v0.35.4 (schema **207**) · **To:** v0.35.5 (schema **207**)

No new migration file. Schema stays **207**. `release_for_schema` still maps 207 to v0.35.1, the release that first shipped that schema.

The published `edgequake-postgres` images for v0.35.5 (pg16, pg17, and pg18) do not contain the Apache AGE library. pgvector 0.8.5, `pg_trgm`, `btree_gin`, and `uuid-ossp` stay. v0.35.4 is the last image that includes AGE.

A data directory created by the v0.35.4 Postgres image has already loaded `age`. The v0.35.5 image has no `age.so`, so Postgres will refuse to open that directory. Use a fresh volume. An existing database that still has the extension must run `edgequake migrate --drop-age` on the v0.35.4 image before the volume moves.

On a server where `age` is not in `pg_available_extensions`, `edgequake migrate` records migration 171 in the same run as the safe schema. Nothing is dropped: migration 170 already marks that database `ready` and `age_absent`. Afterward `/health` reports `pending_count` 0 and `migration_required` false.

On a server where the AGE package is still installed, the default is unchanged. Non-interactive migrate does not drop the extension unless you pass `--drop-age` or set `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATE_DROP_AGE=yes`. Migration 171 stays pending until then.

**SPEC-001 Acc:** medical-mid n=200, archive [`medical-mid-20261016T162456Z`](../../specs/001-benchmark/e2e/artifacts/history/medical-mid-20261016T162456Z/) (`valid: true`). EdgeQuake **0.8054**, LightRAG **0.7920**, delta **+0.0135**, 95% CI **[+0.0056, +0.1506]** (n_paired 40). The harness marks this as not a publishable beat because L2 is incomplete. EdgeQuake does not claim a win. Evidence recall is 0.921 versus 0.956, and context relevancy is 0.437 versus 0.508. The answer prompt is the same as v0.35.4.

```

```bash

curl -sf localhost:8080/health
```

Expect `schema.latest_version` 207, `schema.pending_count` 0, `schema.migration_required` false, and `components.graph_available` true. `pg_available_extensions` has `vector` and does not have `age`.

Existing database that still has Apache AGE, still on the v0.35.4 image:

```bash
edgequake migrate --drop-age
```

Only after that drop succeeds, move the volume or restore the dump onto v0.35.5. Full command reference: [upgrading.md](upgrading.md).

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.7
heading: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.35.7
text:
> **From:** v0.35.5 or v0.35.6 (schema **207**) · **To:** v0.35.7 (schema **207**)

No new migration file. Schema stays **207**. `release_for_schema` still maps 207 to v0.35.1, the release that first shipped that schema. An upgrade from 0.35.5 or 0.35.6 applies no new migration.

A greenfield install does not need Apache AGE. The published Postgres images are the same as v0.35.5: pgvector 0.8.5, `pg_trgm`, `btree_gin`, and `uuid-ossp`, and no Apache AGE. A data directory that already loaded AGE still cannot open on these images. Drop AGE with `edgequake migrate --drop-age` on the v0.35.4 image before moving that volume. See [upgrade-to-0.35.5.md](upgrade-to-0.35.5.md).

A platform admin can switch organization after login. Plain-graph label search recovers typos through the trigram index, and a tenant that does not own the workspace is rejected before lineage or prefix discovery. Neither change needs Apache AGE, and neither changes retrieval scoring.

text:
> **From:** v0.37.0 (schema **218**) · **To:** v0.38.0 (schema **219**)

`edgequake migrate` applies migration **219** only. It creates `mcp_upload_sessions`. It does not move original bytes.

| Migration | What it does |
|-----------|----------------|
| 219 | MCP upload sessions for a checksum-bound agent PUT. Expand only. |

Restart every API replica after migrate so they serve the new binary against schema 219.

A presigned PUT is used when `EDGEQUAKE_ORIGINAL_STORE=object` and the store can sign the content type (and `x-amz-checksum-sha256` on S3). Otherwise the server mints a same-origin HMAC PUT. Set `EDGEQUAKE_MCP_UPLOAD_HMAC_KEY` in production. When that variable is unset, the JWT secret signs the URL. The default JWT secret cannot mint one. `EDGEQUAKE_MCP_UPLOAD_TTL_SECS` is capped at 900. `EDGEQUAKE_MCP_UPLOAD_BIND=bearer` also requires an `Authorization` header.

`edgequake migrate` applies migrations **220** through **224**. All five are expand-only. They do not rewrite documents, chunks, or the graph. Restart every API replica after migrate so they serve the new binary against schema 224.

| Migration | What it does |
|-----------|----------------|
| 220 | Document clearance tables. `enforcement` defaults to false. Existing documents stay readable until a workspace owner turns clearance on. |
| 221 | `model_catalog_policy`. An empty table means unconstrained. Existing workspace model assignments keep running. |
| 222 | Secret-manager tables. The database backend is the default. Infisical is optional and per tenant. Existing connection ciphertext stays readable. |
| 223 | Provider offers. `provider_offer_constrained` defaults to false, so each scope still offers every provider its parent offers. |
| 224 | Provider refresh cache, offer revision, and a unique fleet connection slug. |

Set `EDGEQUAKE_SECRETS_KEY` before anyone saves a new provider key. The server still boots when it is unset. Saving a key without it is refused. Generate a 32-byte key with `openssl rand -base64 32`. Changing the key later makes rows encrypted with the old key unreadable. They are treated as having no key.

Clearance does not hide documents on upgrade. `clearance_covers` is true while the workspace flag is off, including when the settings row is missing.

title: Upgrade to EdgeQuake v0.39.0
heading: What changes for an operator
text:
**Normal RAG workspaces (SPEC-180).** A workspace can now be created as `normal`: chunks, dense embeddings and BM25, with no knowledge graph and no chat model at ingest. The choice is permanent at create time. On a normal workspace the graph endpoints answer `409` and the graph-only retrieval modes answer `422`. Nothing changes for an existing graph workspace.

**Admin consolidation (SPEC-181).** The eight-step create wizards are replaced by two three-decision dialogs, one for an organization and one for a workspace. Platform Admin gains a capability catalog with a single `GET /me/access` answer, a grant editor, and archive/restore. Navigation is gated by the same answer, so a capability an operator does not hold is not rendered.

Three defects are fixed by this cut, and each one matters to an operator who already has data:

- Creating an organization now grants the creator an owner membership. Before, the row existed with no member, so nobody could administer it.
- Deleting an organization now purges all nine storage planes. Before, three were purged and six were orphaned.
- Quota has one source of truth. Before, four different columns disagreed, and `trg_workspace_quota_guard` now enforces the plan limit on write.

`trg_org_keeps_an_owner` refuses the last owner removal from an organization. If your automation revokes memberships, expect that error instead of a silent lockout.

**Provider selection in development (`make dev`).** `make dev` used to export `OLLAMA_HOST` unconditionally. `ProviderFactory::from_env` reads `OLLAMA_HOST` before any cloud key, so an exported `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `XAI_API_KEY` was ignored and the stack ran on Ollama. The Makefile now resolves the provider through `scripts/dev_provider_detect.sh` and exports `EDGEQUAKE_LLM_PROVIDER` / `EDGEQUAKE_LLM_MODEL` explicitly. This affects the local stack only; a deployed container reads the same environment variables as before.

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: Upgrading EdgeQuake
text:
This is the canonical guide to database upgrades. It is for operators who run EdgeQuake on their own PostgreSQL. Read it before you start a newer image or binary. Per-release pages (`upgrade-to-0.XX.md`) describe product changes; this page describes the migration process, which works from any published version to HEAD.

> **Schema train today:** migration **226** (`226_spec181_admin.sql`: `subscription_plans`, real quota columns, archive columns, `scope_purge_receipts`, quota and last-owner triggers). **225** (`225_spec180_normal_rag.sql`: Normal RAG workspace profile columns). **224** (`224_spec179_provider_refresh.sql`: provider refresh). **223** (`223_spec177_provider_offers.sql`: provider offers). `222` is the secret manager. `221` is the model catalog policy. `220` is document clearance. `219` (`219_spec173_mcp_upload_sessions.sql`) is MCP upload sessions. `218` is the PDF window digest. `217` lets page images and extracted markdown live in the object store. `216` adds the originals maintenance role. `215` adds the object-ref ledger. `214_spec169_user_access_links.sql` is the v0.36.0 head (one-time magic and password-reset links). `215`–`226` are expand.
> The released product is **v0.39.1** (schema **226**). v0.39.1 adds no migration. See [upgrade-to-0.39.1.md](upgrade-to-0.39.1.md). The previous product was **v0.39.0** (schema **226**). v0.38.1 through v0.38.4 stopped at **224**. v0.38.0 stopped at **219**. v0.37.0 stopped at **218**. v0.36.0 stopped at **214**. v0.35.7 stopped at **207**. v0.35.0 stopped at **206**. Migration 170 adds plain graph tables. From v0.35.5 the published Postgres image does not include Apache AGE. When `age` is absent from `pg_available_extensions`, `edgequake migrate` records migration 171 in the same run. When the package is installed, 171 still runs only if you pass `--drop-age`. `--confirm-drop` does not answer that question. Migrations 172 through 226 are expand. A v0.35.4 data directory that already loaded AGE cannot open on the v0.35.5 or later image; drop AGE on the v0.35.4 image first. See [upgrade-to-0.39.0.md](upgrade-to-0.39.0.md).
>
> **One rule:** the API never changes the database schema. Only `edgequake migrate` (or the Compose service or Helm Job that runs it) writes schema.

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: Upgrading EdgeQuake
text:
Design detail: [specs/150-reliable-migration-system/](../../specs/150-reliable-migration-system/).
Short reference: [edgequake/docs/migrations.md](../../edgequake/docs/migrations.md).

---

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 1. Which path do I take?
text:
Read your current schema number first (see [section 2](#2-which-version-am-i-on)), then follow the chart.

```mermaid

How to read it: start at the top, answer each question, and stop at the box that matches you. Every path ends with the verify step in section 3.

| From (schema) | Releases | Risk | What to do |
|---------------|----------|------|------------|
| Empty database | none | S | `edgequake migrate` once. A fresh install needs no drop consent. |
| 105 or lower | before v0.23.0 | XL | Backup, check, migrate, drain, then `--confirm-drop` only when the guard is green. |
| 106 to 148 | v0.23.0 to v0.25.x | M to L | Known checksum variants repair automatically. Watch the SPEC-091 guard. See [#396](https://github.com/raphaelmansuy/edgequake/issues/396). |
| 149 | v0.26.x | S to M | Normal path (150 to 169). Leftover drops may still be pending. |
| 159 to 166 | v0.27 to v0.31 | S | Apply the remaining numbered files. |
| 168 | v0.32.x | S | Apply 169 (`provider_connections`, expand-only). |
| 169 | v0.33.0 / v0.34.0 | S | Apply 170 (plain graph). 171 drops AGE only if you answer yes (`--drop-age`). 172 to 207 are expand. |

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 1. Which path do I take?
text:
Risk assumes a small database. Large graphs take longer (class XL) because some steps rewrite AGE tables or build indexes.
Proof: `make spec150-matrix` (all epochs) and `make spec150-matrix-quick` (key epochs) replay each epoch to HEAD on PG16, PG17 and PG18.

---

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 2. Which version am I on?
text:
Ask the running API. If the API is down, ask the migrate CLI (it needs `DATABASE_URL`).

```bash

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: Running API
text: curl -sf localhost:8080/health | jq '{version, schema}'

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: Without the API running (needs DATABASE_URL)
text:
edgequake migrate status    # schema first, then data-engine jobs
edgequake migrate check
```

| Signal | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `version` | Binary or image version, for example `0.32.2`. |
| `schema.latest_version` | Highest applied migration, for example `168`. |
| `schema.pending_count` | Safe-schema migrations still missing. |
| `/ready` returns **200** | Safe for traffic. |
| `/ready` returns **503** | Schema or index not ready. Run migrate, or wait. |

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 3. The golden path (every upgrade)
text:
Run these steps in order. Use the migrator binary or image that matches or is newer than the API you are about to start. Never point an older migrate image at a newer database.

```bash

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 1. Backup
text: pg_dump -Fc "$DATABASE_URL" > edgequake-$(date +%F).dump   # or a volume snapshot

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 6. Check the guard, then drop old tables ONLY when it is green
text:
edgequake migrate guard
edgequake migrate --confirm-drop

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 8. Verify
text:
curl -sf "$HOST/ready" && curl -sf "$HOST/health" | jq .schema
```

The sequence below shows who writes the schema and in what order. The API only reads the ledger.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
sequenceDiagram
  participant Op as Operator
  participant CLI as edgequake migrate
  participant PG as PostgreSQL
  participant API as REST API
  Op->>PG: pg_dump backup
  Op->>CLI: check and dry-run
  CLI->>PG: read-only preflight
  Op->>CLI: migrate
  CLI->>PG: apply safe schema and update ledger
  Op->>CLI: guard
  CLI-->>Op: GREEN or RED
  Op->>CLI: migrate --confirm-drop (only when GREEN)
  CLI->>PG: drop old stores
  Op->>API: start
  API->>PG: read schema ledger (never writes)
  API-->>Op: /ready returns 200
```

Only `edgequake migrate` writes to the database. Steps 1 to 6 happen before the API starts; the API then checks the ledger at boot.

Other `migrate` verbs: `status` (per-job progress), `console [--watch]` (live dashboard), `plan` (ordered runbook), `guard [--family NAME]` (is a flip or drop safe?), `family list|set`, `pause|resume|cancel STEP_ID`. Run `edgequake migrate nonsense` to print the full usage text.

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: What you will see
text:
`edgequake migrate check` and `edgequake migrate` print the upgrade path in plain English. A published v0.34.0 database (schema 169) moving onto this train looks like this:

```text
UPGRADE PATH
  database schema : 169 (≈ v0.33.0)
  binary schema   : 207 (v0.35.0 ≈ v0.35.1)
  pending steps   : 38
  irreversible    : 171 (drops Apache AGE after the SPEC-164 plain-graph ledger is ready)

 APPLY INTENT
  pending total:              38
  SAFE SCHEMA (will apply):   37
  DROP OLD (needs confirm):    1 → 171 (drops Apache AGE after the SPEC-164 plain-graph ledger is ready)
  consent: NOT given — will apply SAFE SCHEMA only, leave DROP OLD pending

migrate ok: pending_before=37 latest=207 applied_this_run=37
```

`latest=207` is the highest applied version. An empty ledger prints `latest=none`. Version lists are spans (`172–207`), not Rust debug dumps. When migration 171 is still waiting for consent, that closing line is followed by `VERDICT: OK TO START THE SERVER`.

Measured on PostgreSQL 16 with 80,000 documents, 40,000 chunks, 30,000 conversations, and 80,000 tasks ([v034_large_upgrade.json](../../specs/164-pure-postgres-study/measurements/v034_large_upgrade.json)):

| Step | Time |
|------|------|
| Empty database, migrations 1–169 | 2.008 s |
| Upgrade 170–202 on that corpus | 3.003 s |
| Document page `status=failed` | 0.081 ms |
| Same page with only the workspace status index visible | 0.051 ms |

The slowest index builds on that corpus (196, 184, 200, 194) each finished in under a second. Row counts were unchanged. Apache AGE was gone after migration 171. Migration-guard CI runs this proof as Layer 4.

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 4. What happens at API boot
text:
The API checks the schema before it serves traffic. The `EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE` setting chooses what it does when migrations are pending.

```mermaid
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#E0E7FF","primaryBorderColor":"#6366F1","primaryTextColor":"#1E1B4B","secondaryColor":"#D1FAE5","secondaryBorderColor":"#10B981","secondaryTextColor":"#064E3B","tertiaryColor":"#FEF3C7","tertiaryBorderColor":"#F59E0B","tertiaryTextColor":"#6B7A90","lineColor":"#7A889C","clusterBkg":"rgba(99,102,241,0.07)","clusterBorder":"#A5B4FC","noteBkgColor":"#FEF9C3","noteTextColor":"#422006","textColor":"#6B7A90","titleColor":"#6B7A90","signalColor":"#7A889C","signalTextColor":"#6B7A90","loopTextColor":"#6B7A90","edgeLabelBackground":"#F1F5F9","actorLineColor":"#94A3B8"}}}%%
%% eq-theme:v1
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Check
  Check --> Serving: schema caught up
  Check --> Refused: pending and gate is fail
  Check --> Waiting: pending and gate is wait
  Check --> Refused: database newer than binary
  Waiting --> Check: poll every 2 seconds
  Refused --> [*]: exit 78
  Serving --> [*]
```

The API starts in `Check`. If the schema is current it serves. If migrations are pending, `fail` mode exits with code 78, while `wait` mode answers `/live` (200) and `/ready` (503) and polls until migrate finishes. A database that is newer than the binary also exits 78.

| Mode | Set it | Use it for |
|------|--------|------------|
| `fail` (default) | nothing | Bare metal and `make dev`. A missing migrate is a loud error. |
| `wait` | `EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE=wait` | Compose and Kubernetes, where migrate and the API start together. |

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 6. Exit codes
text:
| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|-----:|---------|------------|
| 0 | Success. Also returned when only DROP OLD steps remain pending. | Start or keep serving. |
| 1 | Any other migrate error, including an unknown checksum (`VersionMismatch`). The message names the problem. | Read the message, then follow section 7. |
| 75 | Another migrate holds the advisory lock (`MIGRATE_LOCK_BUSY`). | Wait for it. Check `pg_locks`. |
| 78 | Serve refused by the schema gate. | Run `edgequake migrate`, or upgrade the binary if the database is newer. |

---

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 7. Recovery (symptom, cause, fix)
text:
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Migrate fails with `VersionMismatch` (exit 1) | A shipped `NNN_*.sql` was edited, or the database was built from an unlisted variant. | Known variants in `manifest.toml` repair automatically. One time only: `EDGEQUAKE_ALLOW_CHECKSUM_REPAIR=71,78 edgequake migrate`, then unset it. An unknown hash needs a new migration. |
| Migrate stops on a dirty version | A step failed part way. | Inspect `SELECT * FROM public._sqlx_migrations WHERE success = false;`. Fix the DDL or confirm it did not apply, delete the dirty row, rerun `edgequake migrate`. |
| Exit 75 | Two migrates at once, or a crashed session still holds the lock. | Wait up to `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATE_LOCK_DEADLINE` (60 s). After a crash make sure no session holds `hashtext('edgequake.migrate.run')`. |
| `migrate check` fails | Missing `vector` or `age` extension, unsupported PostgreSQL major, binary older than the database, or a dirty ledger. | The command prints a plain-English fix for each. |
| Need to go back | There are no down-migrations. | Restore from backup. Always take a verified backup before `--confirm-drop`. |
| `public._sqlx_migrations` is missing versions that exist in `ag_catalog` or `edgequake` | An older migrator wrote the ledger into the first schema on `search_path`. The DDL committed. The row is the proof. | Re-run `edgequake migrate`. It copies those rows into `public._sqlx_migrations`, drops the stray tables, and prints `ledger: copied N migration row(s) into public._sqlx_migrations and removed stray copies`. |

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 8. Settings for migrate and the gate
text:
Full list: [env-reference.md](env-reference.md). Defaults are read from code.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE` | `fail` | `wait` serves lite `/live` and `/ready` until migrate catches up. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_SCHEMA_GATE_POLL` | `2` | Seconds between polls in wait mode. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATE_LOCK_DEADLINE` | `60` | Seconds to wait for the lock before exit 75. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | `5s` | Session `lock_timeout` for migrate. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT` | unset | Optional override of the session `statement_timeout`. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_ALLOW_CHECKSUM_REPAIR` | unset | Emergency, scoped hash rewrite. Unset it afterwards. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_SERVE_RECONCILE` | unset | One-release escape: allow serve-time support DDL. |
| `EDGEQUAKE_MIGRATION_CONFIRM_DROP` | unset | Same as `--confirm-drop`. Never set it in shared env files. |

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: 9. Known limits
text:
- **[#396](https://github.com/raphaelmansuy/edgequake/issues/396):** the SPEC-091 guard can stay red on mid-cutover fleets. Do not use `--confirm-drop` until it is green.
- **PostgreSQL itself is not upgraded.** Changing the PG major is a separate cluster migration (`scripts/migrate_postgres_major.sh` or an image rebuild).
- **Large graphs.** Some migrations rewrite graph tables or build indexes (for example 070, 071, 074, 156 and 158, plus HNSW builds). On large graphs they can run for a long time. Plan a maintenance window. The 170–202 index steps on an 80,000-document database finished in under a second each; see the measured times in section 3.
- **`migrations/scripts/reset_migrations.sql`** is for development only. It drops the migration ledger. Never run it in production.
- **`edgequake/docker/init.sql`** is legacy and not mounted. The numbered migrations are the schema source of truth.

title: Upgrading EdgeQuake
heading: Vertex project
text:
Image embedding (`gemini-embedding-2`) calls Vertex in one Google Cloud project. A shell that exports a different `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (a common `.zshrc` leftover) sends that call to a project which answers **403**, and the failure used to surface on the last step of creating an image workspace.

`make dev` resolves the project in this order, highest first:

1. `.gcloud_active_project` in the repo root, written by `make gcp-use PROJECT=<id>` or by the first interactive `make dev`.
2. `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`.
3. `PROJECT_ID` (what `gcp-use-mobioos` exports).
4. Unset. Image embedding stays off. Every other provider still works.

A saved file wins over a stray export. Check it with `make vertex-project`. Change it with `make gcp-use PROJECT=<id>`. Forget it with `make vertex-project-forget`; the next interactive `make dev` asks again. Non-interactive runs (`make dev-bg`, CI) never prompt.

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: EdgeQuake product limits

This page tells operators how big a deployment they can promise and what to configure for it. It is for people who size hardware and set vector-search options.

**Rule:** Do not promise a capacity number unless it appears below with evidence.

**Claim gates (lab):** `make ceiling-proof` and `make product-limits-check`. These are lab checks, not day-2 sizing.

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: Status words (read this first)
text:
| Word | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Proven** | Measured under production-style stress (latency + concurrency as claimed) |
| **Supported** | Full claim gate green (filtered ANN Q1-d ∧ recall@20 ∧ concurrent) — safe to promise with the recipe below |
| **Opt-in** | Supported only with an explicit non-default recipe — **no silent flip** |
| **Not promoted** | Lab saw latency or partial wins; do **not** sell as a floor |

**Vectors ≠ documents.** Example: 50 000 chunks at ~100 chunks/doc ≈ **~500 documents**, not 50k docs.

**Promote metric:** **filtered** recall@20 under a workspace filter (`make filtered-recall-gate` / SPEC-075). Never promote from unfiltered-only demos.

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: 1) Default (≤50k) — Proven
text: No special vector flags. Keep the working set resident (`shared_buffers` ≥2 GB).

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: Supported 100k filtered-ANN shape. Use on a new database.
text:
export EDGEQUAKE_VECTOR_STORAGE=halfvec        # already the default when unset
export EDGEQUAKE_HNSW_PARTIAL_BY_WORKSPACE=1   # the opt-in that creates the workspace partial HNSW index
```

`halfvec` is the default storage mode (`VectorStorageMode::from_env`, unset → `halfvec`), so the step that matters for Wave-2 is `EDGEQUAKE_HNSW_PARTIAL_BY_WORKSPACE=1`. Do not change storage or index shape on an existing database without a planned migration.

**Turnkey greenfield (SPEC-071)** — same flags, plus helper + warmup:

```bash
eval "$(make -s wave2-greenfield-env)"

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: or: WAVE2_GREENFIELD=1 make backend-bg
text: ./scripts/wave2_warmup.sh <workspace_uuid>

title: EdgeQuake product limits
heading: or: POST /api/v1/admin/ann/warmup  {"workspace_ids":["<uuid>"]}
text:
```

`/ready` with Wave-2 on checks **catalog** ANN presence (empty DB is ready; tables without HNSW → 503). It is not a plan-shape check. The first filtered query also warms the index if warmup is skipped.

Dedicated `*_ws_*` tables give embedding **dimension** isolation only (SPEC-069). They are **not** the turnkey 100k path.

Clears dedicated concurrent + recall full-gate @**250k** when **`diskann.query_search_list_size ≥ 800`**, **`diskann.query_rescore ≈ list/2`** (e.g. 400), and a higher-quality DiskANN build (SPEC-082: `num_neighbors=64`, `search_list_size=200`). **150 000** still clears the full-gate at **list≥400 / rescore≈200** on the default SBQ build ([SPEC-072](../specs/072-diskann-recall-pareto/e2e/artifacts/RUN_NOTES.md)). heading: SET diskann.query_rescore = 400;            -- ≈ list/2
