heading: What this is
text: [Contents](README.md) · Next: [Sign in and getting around](02-sign-in-and-getting-around.md)

title: What this is
heading: What this is
text:
EdgeQuake turns your files into a map, then answers questions from that map and shows where each part of the answer came from.

You use it in a web browser. The public example is [https://demo.edgequake.com/](https://demo.edgequake.com/). After you [sign in](02-sign-in-and-getting-around.md), the left sidebar is the whole product:

- **Dashboard** is the home page. It shows how many files and map items you have.
- **Documents** is the file list. You drop PDFs here.
- **Query** is where you ask a question in a box and read the answer.
- **Knowledge Graph** is the map itself: dots and lines you can click.
- **Knowledge** is where you type extra notes, such as a glossary, that the map should also know.
- **Workspace** is the settings for one collection of files: which model reads them, and how they are split.
- **Pipeline** is the work queue. It shows files waiting, files being read, and files that finished.
- **Costs** is the bill for the model calls in this collection.
- **API Explorer** is the same product written as web requests, for people who want a program to talk to it.
- **Settings** is your own look and feel, plus the connections to model providers.

The header, on every page, shows which organization and which workspace you are in. On the demo that line reads **Default — Default Workspace**. The green dot and **API v0.36.0** mean the server behind the page is up. The pictures in this tour were taken there. The screens themselves are the same in the release that ships this tour.

A typical visit is short. You look at the [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md), open a file under [Documents](04-documents.md), ask something on [Query](06-ask-a-question.md), then click a dot on [the map](07-the-map.md) to see why the answer mentioned that name.

title: What this is
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Sign in and getting around](02-sign-in-and-getting-around.md). If you already have an account, the [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md) is the first page you land on.

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: Sign in and getting around
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [What this is](01-what-this-is.md) · Next: [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md)

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: Sign in and getting around
text:
Open [https://demo.edgequake.com/](https://demo.edgequake.com/). If you are not signed in, you get a single card.

![The sign-in card. Username and password are empty. The button says Sign In.](images/02-sign-in.png)

The card has two boxes and one button:

- **Username** is the account name. On this demo the administrator account is `admin`.
- **Password** is the secret that matches that name. The eye on the right of the box shows or hides what you typed. Leave it hidden.
- **Sign In** checks those two values and opens the [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md).

Type the username and password you were given. This tour does not print a password.

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: The sidebar
text:
After you sign in, a column stays on the left on every page. The top is the EdgeQuake logo, which always returns to the Dashboard. Then four everyday items: **Dashboard**, **Documents**, **Query**, **Knowledge Graph**. Under the label **KNOWLEDGE** are **Knowledge** and **Workspace**. Under the label **SYSTEM** are **Pipeline**, **Costs**, **API Explorer**, and **Settings**.

The black pill is the page you are on. **Collapse**, at the bottom of the column, shrinks the names to icons. The footer of the column shows **EdgeQuake** and **UI v0.36.0**, which is the website build in these pictures.

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: The header
text:
The thin bar across the top has four things:

- The chip **Default — Default Workspace** is the organization and the collection you are looking at. Click it to switch.
- The green **API v0.36.0** is the server. Green means it answered a health check.
- The globe changes the language of the labels.
- The sun or moon switches light and dark.
- The person icon is the user menu, including sign out.

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: Switching organization or workspace
text:
Click the chip. A small panel opens over the Dashboard.

![The switcher open on the Dashboard. Organization Default is checked. Workspace Default Workspace is checked. Create New Tenant and Create New Workspace sit under each list.](images/02-workspace-switcher.png)

The panel has a search box, then two lists:

1. **Organization.** This is the tenant. **Default** is checked, with the subtitle **System Default Tenant**. **Create New Tenant** starts a new organization. On a shared demo, leave that alone.
2. **Workspace.** **Default Workspace** is checked. The short name under it is `default`. **Create New Workspace** starts another collection of files inside the same organization.

A checkmark is the one you are in. Pick a row to move. Press Escape, or click outside the panel, to close it without changing anything.

The rest of this tour stays inside **Default — Default Workspace**.

title: Sign in and getting around
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md). The same sidebar is on every later page, so later chapters name only what is new on that screen. The [Workspace](09-workspaces.md) page is where you change how that collection is read.

title: Dashboard
heading: Dashboard
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Sign in and getting around](02-sign-in-and-getting-around.md) · Next: [Documents](04-documents.md)

title: Dashboard
heading: Dashboard
text:
The Dashboard is the home page. It answers one question: how big is this workspace, and is it healthy?

![The Dashboard for Default Workspace. Four count cards sit on top, three shortcut buttons under them, and a list of recent files below.](images/03-dashboard.png)

The title is the workspace name, **Default Workspace**. The line under it, **All documents are processed**, means every file has been read. If something were still running, that line would say so and you would open [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md).

title: Dashboard
heading: The four counts
text:
- **Documents** — **15**. These are the uploaded files. The caption says **Uploaded documents**.
- **Entities** — **13,200**. These are the things pulled out of the files. The caption says **Extracted entities**.
- **Relationships** — **12,023**. These are the lines between those things. The caption says **Entity connections**.
- **Chunks** — **591**. These are the short pieces the files were cut into. The caption says **Text segments**.

The numbers are for the workspace in the header chip. Switch workspace and the cards change.

title: Dashboard
heading: The three shortcuts
text:
- **Upload Documents** — "Add new documents to your knowledge base." This opens [Documents](04-documents.md).
- **Query Knowledge** — "Ask questions about your data." This opens [Query](06-ask-a-question.md).
- **View Graph** — "Explore entity relationships." This opens [the map](07-the-map.md).

title: Dashboard
heading: Recent activity
text:
**Recent Activity** lists the latest uploads. Each row is a file name, how long ago it arrived, and a green **Completed** pill. On this day the top rows included `terra-incognita-public-20261015.pdf` and `math_2610.19864v1.pdf`.

The green pill at the right of the heading says **All systems operational · openai**. That is the model provider the server is using for answers right now.

**View all 15 documents** at the bottom jumps to the full file list.

title: Dashboard
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Documents](04-documents.md). If you would rather ask a question first, go to [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md).

title: Documents
heading: Documents
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md) · Next: [One document](05-one-document.md)

title: Documents
heading: Documents
text:
Documents is the library. You add files here, and you see whether each one has been turned into map items.

![The Documents page. A drop zone sits above a table of 15 files, each marked Ready.](images/04-documents.png)

The heading is **Documents** with a count, **12**, and a green dot. The subtitle is **Upload and manage documents for knowledge graph extraction**.

title: Documents
heading: Adding a file
text:
The dashed box is the drop zone. It says **Drop files or choose them**. You can drag a file onto it, or click and pick one from your computer. The note under the box says files can be up to 50MB, and Word and Excel files are not accepted. PDF and text are the usual choices.

Three menus sit in that same box:

- **Workspace (Vision)** chooses the model that looks at page pictures.
- **Workspace (LLM)** chooses the model that reads the text and lists entities.
- **Vision** chooses how a PDF is read. Vision means a model looks at each page as a picture, which is the right choice for scans, tables, and figures.

**Upload** in the toolbar opens or closes this box. **Refresh** reloads the list. **Layout** changes how the list is drawn. The **⋯** menu holds less common actions.

On a shared demo, do not upload a private file. The drop zone is there so you can see how adding a file works.

title: Documents
heading: The library
text:
**Library** and the count **12** sit above the table. **Search documents...** filters by name. **All Status (12)** filters by state. **Created** and **Updated** change the sort.

The columns are:

- A checkbox, for acting on several rows at once.
- **Title**, the file name.
- **Status**. **Ready** in green means the file was read and the map was updated. The fuller label is **Completed · Ready**.
- **Entities**, how many things were found in that file. The bricks paper shows **1965**.
- **Created** and **Last Updated**, as a relative time such as **2 days ago**.
- A **⋯** menu on the row for actions on that one file.

The footer says **1–12 of 12**, **Rows per page** (here **100**), and page **1 / 1**.

Click a row once and a preview opens on the right. Double-click a row and you get the full page for that file, which is the next chapter.

title: Documents
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [One document](05-one-document.md). When many files are still being read, the place to watch is [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md).

title: One document
heading: One document
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Documents](04-documents.md) · Next: [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md)

title: One document
heading: One document
text: A document has two views. A short preview sits beside the list. The full page shows the extracted text, the counts, and the steps that produced them.

title: One document
heading: The preview
text:
Click a row once on [Documents](04-documents.md). A panel named **Document Preview** opens on the right. You can close it with the **×**.

![The library with the preview open for terra-incognita-public-20261015.pdf. The panel shows Completed, 992 entities, a cost of $0.07, and the start of the extracted text.](images/05-document-preview.png)

For `terra-incognita-public-20261015.pdf` the panel shows:

- A green **Completed** pill, **992 entities**, and **1 day ago**.
- **Details**: an **ID** you can copy, plus **Created** and **Updated**.
- **Processing cost**: **Total Cost $0.07**, **Total Tokens 205.7K**, split into **Input Tokens 113.5K** and **Output Tokens 92.2K**, the **LLM Model** `mistral-small-latest`, and the **Embedding** model `mistral-embed`.
- **Content preview** of the paper title and author, with **View Details** and **Graph** at the bottom.

This is a glance. The full page is where you read the file.

title: One document
heading: The full page
text:
Click **View Details** in the preview (or open the document URL). The address changes to a page for that one document. The list view with the same preview open is shown below; the reader layout is the same pattern on every file.

![Documents list with terra-incognita-public-20261015.pdf selected and Document Preview open on the right.](images/05-document.png)

The toolbar on the document page has:

- A download icon, which saves the file.
- **Ask**, which opens [Query](06-ask-a-question.md) with this file in mind.
- **Reprocess specific pages**, which sends chosen pages through reading again.
- **Reprocess**, which sends the whole file through again.

Use those reprocess buttons only on a collection you own. They spend model calls and rewrite the map for this file.

title: One document
heading: The reader
text:
The middle is the text the software extracted. Page controls sit above the text:

- Page arrows move between pages.
- The magnifying glasses and zoom percentage zoom in and out.
- **Layout** changes the arrangement.
- **Extracted Markdown** is the text you are looking at. Markdown is the simple text format the reader uses, with headings and pictures.
- **None**, **PDF → MD**, and **MD → PDF** choose what you compare. **PDF → MD** is the useful one: the original page on one side and the extracted text on the other.

title: One document
heading: The details column
text: **Details** on the right has tiles for **Chunks**, **Entities**, **Relations**, and how long processing took. **Extraction Lineage** is the path from the file to the map: upload, PDF → Markdown (Vision), content extraction, entity extraction, and relationship mapping. If a step had failed, this column is where you would see it.

title: One document
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md). To see this file's entities as dots, open [the map](07-the-map.md) and search for a name you saw in the text.

title: Ask a question
heading: Ask a question
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [One document](05-one-document.md) · Next: [The map](07-the-map.md)

title: Ask a question
heading: Ask a question
text:
Query is the chat. You type a question. EdgeQuake looks through the workspace and answers with notes that point back at the files.

![The empty Query page. Four example questions sit in the middle. History is the list on the right. The question box is at the bottom.](images/06-query.png)

The heading is **Query**, with the subtitle **Ask questions about your knowledge graph**.

**New** starts a blank conversation. The icon buttons beside it show the map next to the chat, show or hide the **History** list, and open extra settings for this question (how many sources to keep, and whether the answer streams in as it is written).

title: Ask a question
heading: The empty page
text:
Before you ask anything, the page offers four examples:

- What are the main entities in my knowledge graph?
- Summarize the key relationships between documents
- Find connections between people and organizations
- What topics are covered in my documents?

Click one and it is sent as your question.

title: Ask a question
heading: The question box
text:
The box at the bottom says **Ask a question... type @ to focus on a document**.

- Type a question and press **Enter** to send. **Shift+Enter** adds a line without sending.
- Type **@** to limit the question to one file, so the answer does not wander across the whole library.
- **All docs** means every file in the workspace is allowed. Click it to pick a smaller set.
- **Smart** is the way the search runs. Open it to see the other five. The next section lists them.
- **gpt-5.6-terra** is the model that will write the answer. Click it to pick another model this workspace is allowed to use.
- The paper-plane button sends the question.

title: Ask a question
heading: The six ways to search
text:
Click **Smart** and a menu titled **Retrieval mode** opens. Each row is a way of looking things up. The short name is what you click. The words in parentheses are the name a program sends to the server. You only need the short name.

![The retrieval menu open. Smart is checked and marked Recommended. The other rows are Focused, Broad, Linked, Chunks, and Chat.](images/06-query-modes.png)

- **Focused** (`local`). Looks up one entity and the lines and chunks next to it. Use it when you already know the name: a person, a product, a paper.
- **Broad** (`global`). Follows themes that run across files. Use it for "how do these documents connect?"
- **Linked** (`hybrid`). Runs Focused and Broad together, and also looks at chunks, then merges what it found.
- **Smart** (`mix`). Recommended, and the one with the checkmark. Runs Focused, Broad, and chunk search at the same time, then ranks them into one pile. This is the right default for most questions.
- **Chunks** (`naive`). Looks only at the pieces of the files, using similarity and keywords. It does not walk the map. Use it when you want a sentence or a number copied from a page.
- **Chat** (`bypass`). Does not look anything up. The question goes straight to the model. Use it for a general question that should ignore your files.

Close the menu with Escape. **Smart** is already selected on the demo.

title: Ask a question
heading: History
text:
**History** on the right is every conversation in this workspace. **Search conversations...** filters the titles. **Unfiled** is the folder that holds conversations you have not filed. **New Folder** makes a folder. The list is grouped into **Today**, **Yesterday**, and **Previous 7 days**. Each row is a title and a time, such as **Main Entities in Knowledge Graph**.

Click a row to read that conversation again. That does not send a new question.

title: Ask a question
heading: An answer
text:
This is an existing conversation, opened from History. The question was **What are the main entities in my knowledge graph?**

![The answer, scrolled to the summary. Source chips name a PDF and a page. Under the summary are numbered sources, a strength line, and the question box.](images/06-answer.png)

Read it from the top of the conversation (scroll up if you land in the middle):

- Your question is the first bubble.
- The answer is the long text under it. Names in the answer are links into the files. A chip such as `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash_...pdf` plus a page number is one of those links. Click it to open that place in the [document](05-one-document.md).
- **Summary** is the short version at the end of the answer.
- **Sources** under the summary are numbered chips, **[1] [2] [3] [4]** and **+5 more**. Each chip is a file or a passage the answer used.
- The line **9 Sources · 0 Topics** counts what was attached. **Strong (100%)** is a rough grade of how well the answer stayed on those sources. It is a hint, not a proof.
- The small icons under the answer copy the text, ask the model to write it again, and share or export it.

The same question box stays at the bottom, so the next question continues this conversation. **New** starts over.

title: Ask a question
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [The map](07-the-map.md). The sources on an answer are the same entities you can click there.

title: The map
heading: The map
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md) · Next: [Extra knowledge](08-extra-knowledge.md)

title: The map
heading: The map
text:
Knowledge Graph is the picture of the workspace. Each dot is an entity. Each line is a relationship. The sidebar calls this page **Knowledge Graph**.

The demo map is large: **13,200** dots and many thousands of lines. The page draws a sample so the browser stays usable. The orange bar at the bottom says **200 of 13,200 nodes (2%)**. **Load More** asks for the next batch.

![The map, with 200 dots drawn. A list of entities is on the left, filters are on the right, and a Neighbourhood card offers 1 hop, 2 hops, and 3 hops.](images/07-graph.png)

title: The map
heading: The entity list
text:
The left column is titled **ENTITIES** with the count **200** (the ones currently drawn). **Search entities...** filters that list as you type. **Sort** is **Name** or **Degree**. Degree is how many lines touch that dot. **Grouped** bunches them by kind. **List** is one flat list.

Each row is a name, a kind such as **Artifact**, and a number. **Deepseek-V4.1-Flash** is an Artifact with **130** connections. Click a row to select that dot. The right-hand **Details** panel fills in, and the map moves to that dot.

title: The map
heading: The canvas
text:
The center title is **Knowledge Graph**, with **200 nodes · 549 edges** for the sample on screen.

The toolbar on that title row, from left to right after the title:

- **Search nodes...** finds a dot by name. The **×** clears the search.
- The table icon switches the dots to a table. Click it again to come back to the picture.
- The badge **200 / 13,200 (2%)** is the same "how much is drawn" count as the orange bar.
- The layout control and **Apply Layout** place the dots again.
- **Export** downloads a picture of the map.
- **Refresh** reloads the dots from the server.
- The settings icon opens picture options for this view (the same ideas as **Graph Visualization** on [Settings](13-settings.md)).
- The keyboard icon lists shortcut keys.
- **Zoom in**, **Zoom out**, and **Fit to screen** change the camera. The same three sit on the right edge of the picture.

Around the canvas:

- The **+** and **−** buttons zoom in and out. The fit button scales the map so the drawn dots all fit.
- **Neighbourhood** chooses how far to walk when you focus on one dot. **1 hop** is the dots one line away. **2 hops** and **3 hops** go further. The card says **Click a node to focus on its neighbourhood**.
- The small overview square in the corner is the whole sample, with a rectangle for the part you are looking at.

Colors match kinds of entity. The right-hand **FILTERS** list is the legend:

- **Search entities or types...** filters the legend.
- **ENTITY TYPES** says **11 types** and **200 of 200 nodes visible**.
- Each row is a color, a name, a count, and an eye. The eye hides or shows that kind. On this day the counts included **Artifact 45**, **Concept 33**, **Content 30**, **Method 28**, **Organization 16**, **Other 16**, **Person 13**, **Event 8**, **Data 6**, **Drawing 4**, and **Creature 1**.
- **Hide all** turns every kind off. Click the eyes again to bring them back.

**DOCUMENT** and **All entities** above the canvas limit the dots to one file or show every file.

Until you click a dot, **Details** says **Select a node** and **Click any node to explore its connections and sources**.

title: The map
heading: One dot
text:
Click **Deepseek-V4.1-Flash** in the list. The row turns black, the map centers on that dot, and **Details** fills in.

![Deepseek-V4.1-Flash selected. The Details panel shows the type Artifact, a short description, and properties such as the source document.](images/07-graph-node.png)

The panel shows:

- The name **Deepseek-V4.1-Flash** and a pill **Artifact**.
- **DESCRIPTION**. Here it is a short line about a multimodal model from DeepSeek.
- **PROPERTIES**. **description** repeats that line. **source_chunk_ids** and **source_document_id** are the ids of the chunk and the file this fact was read from. **logical_node_id** is the map's own name for the dot, in capitals: `DEEPSEEK-V4.1-FLASH`. **entity_type** is **ARTIFACT**.
- **Copy All** copies those properties.

The icons next to the name open the same entity in other views, including the file it came from. That is the same trail you see on a [document](05-one-document.md) and on an [answer](06-ask-a-question.md).

The Neighbourhood card may still be open. **0 nodes in reach** on a tight zoom means the walk has not been applied yet. Pick **1 hop** to pull in the neighbours.

title: The map
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Extra knowledge](08-extra-knowledge.md). The models that decide which kinds of dots exist are set on [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md).

title: Extra knowledge
heading: Extra knowledge
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [The map](07-the-map.md) · Next: [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md)

title: Extra knowledge
heading: Extra knowledge
text:
Knowledge is a notebook you write yourself. A glossary, a list of acronyms, or a definition you want the map to respect goes here. The sidebar label is **Knowledge**. The page title is **Knowledge Injection**.

The demo has none yet, so the page is an empty state. That is useful: you can see the invitation without anyone else's notes in the way.

![The empty Knowledge page. A book icon, the line No knowledge injections yet, and a button Create your first injection.](images/08-knowledge.png)

The subtitle under the title says **Inject domain glossaries, acronyms, and definitions to enrich your knowledge graph.**

**New Injection**, at the top right, and **Create your first injection**, in the middle, open the same form. The empty-state sentence says injected knowledge improves search and does not show up as a citation. An answer can use the glossary, and the source chips still point at documents, not at this note.

title: Extra knowledge
heading: The form
text:
![The Create Knowledge Injection dialog. Text is selected. Name and Content are empty, with an example glossary in the Content placeholder. Cancel and Create are at the bottom.](images/08-knowledge-new.png)

- **Text** means you type the note. **File** means you upload a text file instead.
- **Name** is a label, with the example **Manufacturing Glossary**.
- **Content** is the note. The placeholder shows a short example: OEE as Overall Equipment Effectiveness, and MTBF as Mean Time Between Failures. The counter reads **0 / 102,400 characters**.
- **Cancel** closes the form and saves nothing. **Create** stores the note in this workspace.

On the shared demo, press **Cancel**. Creating a note would change the public workspace.

After a note exists, it appears in the list on this page. You can come back and edit it. It applies to the workspace shown in the header chip, the same collection as [Documents](04-documents.md) and [the map](07-the-map.md).

title: Extra knowledge
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md). Questions that should use this extra context are asked on [Query](06-ask-a-question.md).

title: Workspaces
heading: Workspaces
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Extra knowledge](08-extra-knowledge.md) · Next: [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md)

title: Workspaces
heading: Workspaces
text:
Workspace is the control page for one collection. The [Dashboard](03-dashboard.md) tells you how big the collection is. This page tells you which models read it, how files are split, and which buttons would rebuild or delete it.

The picture is the whole page, top to bottom. Read it in that order. The header chip still says which collection you are editing. Here it is **Default Workspace**.

![The Workspace page, from the four counts at the top through model cards, chunking, entity types, rebuild buttons, and the red Danger Zone at the bottom.](images/09-workspace.png)

title: Workspaces
heading: The title row
text:
**Default Workspace** has an **Active** pill and the subtitle **Default knowledge base**. **Refresh** reloads the page. **Edit Configuration** opens the editor for the name and the model choices.

Four cards repeat the Dashboard counts: **Documents 15**, **Entities 13200**, **Relationships 12023**, **Chunks 591**.

title: Workspaces
heading: Which model does what
text:
Three cards name the models for this collection. A **Workspace Override** badge means this collection uses its own choice, not only the server default.

- **LLM Configuration** is the model that lists entities and writes summaries while a file is read. Here it is `mistral-small-latest`, which resolves to `mistral/mistral-small-latest`. **Extract effort** and **Query effort** are both **Auto → omit**, which means "leave the model's own effort setting alone".
- **Embedding Configuration** is the model that turns chunks into vectors, long lists of numbers that let similar text be found. Here it is `mistral-embed`, **1024** dimensions, resolving to `mistral/mistral-embed`.
- **Vision LLM (PDF Extraction)** is the model that looks at PDF pages. Here it is `magistral-small-latest`.

**PDF Parser** chooses how new PDFs are read. **Server Default (Vision)** means "use whatever the server is set to", and the server is currently **Vision**. The card says EdgeParse is the fast path for ordinary digital PDFs, and Vision is the better path for scans and pages that are mostly pictures.

title: Workspaces
heading: How files are cut up
text:
These cards apply to files you add from now on. Files already in the library stay as they are until you rebuild.

- **Extraction Language** is **Server default (English)**. Entity names and descriptions are written in that language.
- **Chunking** is **Fixed · 1200/100**. Files are cut into pieces of about 1200 tokens, with 100 tokens of overlap so a sentence on the boundary is not lost. The card also says markdown headings and short PDF pages are packed together so a heading is not its own lonely chunk.
- **Extract budget** is **Custom · 40/100**. One model reply may list at most 40 entities and 100 rows in total. This is a cap on a single reply, not a cap on the whole map.

title: Workspaces
heading: Extraction mode
text:
**Extraction mode** is **LLM**, marked **Active**, on **Server default (LLM)**. A chat model reads each chunk and lists entities and relations.

Under that is **Decision engine**. It is a second, optional reader that answers yes-or-no questions with a small local model. On this demo it is set to **Ollama** at `host.docker.internal:11434` and the model `tev1:0.8b`. The yellow line **Cannot reach the decision backend** means that small model is not running on the demo server. **Check again** retries. The chat-model path above it is the one actually reading documents. **Advanced** hides extra knobs. **Reset** and **Save** apply to this card. Leave them unless you are configuring your own server.

title: Workspaces
heading: What kinds of things are allowed
text:
**Entity Types** lists the kinds of dots the reader may create. This workspace uses the server defaults: **PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, EVENT, CONCEPT, TECHNOLOGY, PRODUCT, DATE, DOCUMENT**. **Strict limit: on** means a thing that fits none of those becomes **OTHER**.

**Relation Types** lists the kinds of lines: **RELATED_TO**, **PART_OF**, **LOCATED_IN**, **WORKS_AT**, **CREATED_BY**. Under them, **Typed edges** shows which kinds of dots may use which line, for example **PERSON — WORKS_AT → ORGANIZATION**. **+2 more** expands the rest.

title: Workspaces
heading: Rebuild and delete
text:
**Workspace Actions** is the dangerous half of the page. Read it before you click.

- **Rebuild Embeddings** recomputes vectors. The card shows the current model `mistral/mistral-embed` and dimension **1024**. Use it after you change the embedding model. It does not delete the entities.
- **Rebuild Knowledge Graph** clears the entities and relationships and reads the files again. Use it after you change the chat model, the entity types, or the chunk size. It deletes the current map for this workspace. Documents stay.
- The id line shows **Workspace ID**, the short name **default**, and **Created** / **Updated** **9/19/2026**.
- The green line **Workspace ready for queries and document ingestion** means you can ask questions and add files.
- **Danger Zone** and **Delete this workspace** remove the collection, including documents, entities, relationships, and embeddings. That cannot be undone. On the demo, do not press it.

title: Workspaces
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md). The day-to-day switches for pictures and answers, including theme and saved connections, are on [Settings](13-settings.md).

title: Pipeline
heading: Pipeline
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md) · Next: [Costs](11-costs.md)

title: Pipeline
heading: Pipeline
text:
Pipeline is the work queue. When you add a file on [Documents](04-documents.md), this page is where you watch it move from waiting, to being read, to finished.

On the day of the picture every file was already finished, so the page is quiet. That is the normal look of a healthy workspace.

![Pipeline Status for Default Workspace. Pending, Processing, and Failed are 0. Completed is 15. The progress bar is full.](images/10-pipeline.png)

The title is **Pipeline Status**, with **Default Workspace** under it. **Back to Documents** returns to the library. **Refresh** reloads the counts.

title: Pipeline
heading: Document pipeline
text:
The card **Document Pipeline** says **15 documents in workspace** and a green **Idle** pill. Idle means nothing is running.

Four tiles:

- **Pending 0** — files waiting for a turn.
- **Processing 0** — files being read right now.
- **Completed 15** — files that finished. This tile is green.
- **Failed 0** — files that stopped with an error. If this number is not zero, open the file from [Documents](04-documents.md) and read the lineage column.

**Pipeline Progress** is the bar under the tiles: **15 / 15 completed**.

title: Pipeline
heading: The rest of the page
text:
**Chunk Progress** is the finer view, one piece of a file at a time. It says **No active chunk progress** while the queue is idle.

**Active Documents** lists files that are queued or being read. It says **No queued or processing documents**.

**Queue Metrics** describes the workers that do the reading:

- **Workers 0/4 (0%)** — none of the four slots are busy.
- **Throughput < 0.1/min** — almost nothing is finishing per minute, because nothing is in flight.
- **Avg Wait 2s** — a typical wait before a job starts.
- **Queue ETA 0s** — estimated time left.
- **Queue: 0 pending**.

**Activity Log** would list recent events. It says **No recent activity**.

**Advanced Details** opens a longer technical dump. You can leave it closed.

When you upload a file on your own server, come back here and refresh until **Completed** matches the number of files and **Failed** stays at zero.

title: Pipeline
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Costs](11-costs.md). The models this queue calls are chosen on [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md).

title: Costs
heading: Costs
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md) · Next: [API Explorer](12-api-explorer.md)

title: Costs
heading: Costs
text:
Costs is the bill for model calls in this workspace. Reading a file and answering a question both call a model, and both show up here.

![The Cost Dashboard. Total cost is $1.76 across 15 documents. Extraction is most of the bar. A token table sits at the bottom.](images/11-costs.png)

The title is **Cost Dashboard**. The subtitle on the screen is **Monitor LLM costs and usage across your workspace**. LLM is the language model: the program that reads files and writes answers.

**Last 30 days** is the range for the trend chart. The refresh icon reloads the numbers. **Download** saves the table.

title: Costs
heading: The summary
text:
**Cost Summary**, labeled **All time**, has four figures for this demo:

- **Total Cost $1.76**
- **Documents 15**
- **Avg per Document $0.117**
- **Tokens Used 4.4M**

A token is a small piece of text the model is billed on. A short sentence is a handful of tokens. 4.4 million is the sum of everything sent in and everything the model wrote back.

**Budget Status** is a monthly cap. It shows **$0.00 of $100.00**, **0% used**, and **$100.00 remaining**. The **Monthly** pill and **Resets in** tell you the cap is per month. The $1.76 in the summary is all-time spend, so it can be higher than the month-to-date number in the budget card. On this day the current month had not added new spend.

title: Costs
heading: Where the money went
text:
**Cost Breakdown**, total **$1.76**:

- **Extraction $1.58**, the blue bar, about **90%**. This is the work of reading files and listing entities.
- **Embedding $0.176**, the purple bar, about **10%**. This is the work of turning chunks into vectors.

**Cost Trend** is a chart of spend across days. The labels along the bottom are dates. A flat chart means little new work in that window.

title: Costs
heading: The token table
text:
**Token Usage Details** says **4.4M total tokens**. The columns are **Stage**, **Input**, **Output**, **Calls**, and **Cost**.

| Stage | Input | Output | Calls | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Extraction | 2.1M | 2.3M | 15 | $1.58 |
| Embedding | 0 | 0 | 15 | $0.176 |
| Total | 2.1M | 2.3M | 30 | $1.76 |

Input is text sent to the model. Output is text the model returned. Embedding shows zeros in the token columns and still shows a cost, because that provider bills the vector step differently. **Calls** is how many times that stage ran: 15, once per document, and 30 in total.

These figures belong to the public demo. Your own workspace will show your own bill.

title: Costs
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [API Explorer](12-api-explorer.md). The queue that generates most of this bill is [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md).

title: API Explorer
heading: API Explorer
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Costs](11-costs.md) · Next: [Settings](13-settings.md)

title: API Explorer
heading: API Explorer
text:
API Explorer is the same product, written as requests a program can send. You do not need it to use the website. Open it when you want to see the exact call behind a button, or when you are writing a script.

![API Explorer. Health is expanded on the left, with three GET entries. The introduction on the right explains the two headers every call sends.](images/12-api-explorer.png)

The title is **API Explorer**. Under it is the address of the description file, `https://demo.edgequake.com/api-docs/openapi.json`. **Open in Swagger UI** opens the same description in another layout, in a new tab.

**Search**, with the hint **⌘K**, filters the list on the left.

title: API Explorer
heading: The list
text:
Each row is a group of calls. A chevron opens the group. **Health** is open in the picture. Inside it:

- **Deep health check with component status**, a **GET** (a read-only request). This is the check behind the green **API v0.36.0** dot in the header.
- **Liveness check (for Kubernetes)**, also a **GET**. A simple "the process is up". Kubernetes is the system that runs the demo server.
- **Readiness check (for Kubernetes)**, a **GET**. A simple "the process can take work".

Other groups match the screens you have already seen: **Documents**, **Query**, **Graph**, **Entities**, **Relationships**, **Pipeline**, **Tasks**, **Costs**, **Tenants**, **Workspaces**, **Conversations**, **Authentication**, **API Keys**, and more. Click a row to read the inputs and outputs of that one call.

The footer of the list says **Powered by Scalar**, which is the component that draws this page.

title: API Explorer
heading: The introduction
text:
The right-hand pane is the overview:

- A badge **v0.36.0** and **OpenAPI 3.1.0**. OpenAPI is the standard format of the description file.
- **EdgeQuake API**, **Download OpenAPI Document**, and a one-line summary.
- **Context Headers**. Almost every call needs two headers. **X-Tenant-ID** is the organization. **X-Workspace-ID** is the workspace. The website sets both when you pick **Default — Default Workspace** in the header. The example box shows the all-zero sample ids used in the documentation, not a secret.
- **Server** is a menu of base addresses. **http://localhost:8080** is the usual address on your own machine. The demo you are looking at is `https://demo.edgequake.com`.
- **Authentication** says what the call must carry. On this server that is a bearer token (the proof you signed in) plus the tenant id and the workspace id.

You can try a call from this page. A call that creates, deletes, or reprocesses data will change the demo. Stick to the **GET** health calls if you are only looking.

title: API Explorer
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Settings](13-settings.md). Asking a question from the website, which is the same idea as the Query calls in this list, is covered in [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md).

title: Settings
heading: Settings
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [API Explorer](12-api-explorer.md) · Next: [The copilot](14-copilot.md)

title: Settings
heading: Settings
text:
Settings is the long page of preferences. The top is how the website looks. The middle is which model servers EdgeQuake may call. The bottom is how the map is drawn and how questions are asked. Scroll the page. The pictures below are slices of that one scroll.

Nothing here deletes your documents. The red buttons at the bottom clear saved questions or reset these switches. The button that deletes a workspace is on [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md), not here.

title: Settings
heading: Appearance
text:
![The top of Settings. Theme is System. Language is English. Application Attribution has App ID, App Name, and App URL.](images/13-settings.png)

The title is **Settings**, subtitle **Customize your EdgeQuake experience**.

**Appearance**:

- **Theme** is **System**, **Light**, or **Dark**. System follows your computer.
- **Language** is the language of the labels. Here it is **English**. The globe in the header changes the same setting.

**Application Attribution** is a name the server can send along with model calls, so the provider's logs show who the caller was. **App ID** is `edgequake`, **App Name** is `EdgeQuake`, **App URL** is an address such as `http://localhost:3000`. **Save attribution** stores those three. The **Provider header catalog** under the button is a reference table: for each provider, which headers are sent. You do not edit that table. It is there so you can see that OpenAI gets one header, Anthropic gets another, and so on.

Further down the same page, still above the connections, are the server-wide model defaults and a priority switch. **Server first** means a value saved in Settings wins over an environment variable. **Environment first** means the variable wins. The page prints the effective model, for example the chat model and the embedding model the server is using right now. Leave those dropdowns alone on the demo.

title: Settings
heading: How the map is drawn
text:
![Graph Visualization. Show Node Labels is on. Show Edge Labels is off. Node Size is Medium. Default Layout is ForceAtlas2.](images/13-settings-graph.png)

**Graph Visualization** changes [the map](07-the-map.md) only. It does not change the data.

- **Show Node Labels** prints the name on each dot. It is on.
- **Show Edge Labels** prints the relationship type on each line. It is off, which keeps a crowded map readable.
- **Node Size** is **Small**, **Medium**, or **Large**. It is **Medium**.
- **Default Layout** is the algorithm that places the dots. It is **ForceAtlas2 (FA2)**, which pulls connected dots together and pushes the rest apart.

The cards just above this one on the scroll, **Vision LLM Default** and **Workspace Embeddings**, repeat what [Workspaces](09-workspaces.md) already shows: the vision model `magistral-small-latest`, and **Rebuild Embeddings** for `mistral/mistral-embed` at dimension **1024**.

title: Settings
heading: How questions behave
text:
![Query Defaults and Ingestion Settings. Default query mode is Smart. Streaming and reranking are on. Gleaning and LLM summarization are on.](images/13-settings-query.png)

**Query Defaults**:

- **Default Query Mode** is **Smart · Recommended**. That is the same **Smart** choice explained in [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md). New conversations start here. You can still change it for one question from the menu on the question box.
- **Enable Streaming** is on. The answer appears as it is written, instead of all at once at the end.
- **Enable Reranking** is on. After the search finds a pile of passages, a second step reorders them so the closer ones come first.
- **Rerank Top K** is **10**. Ten passages survive that second step.

**Ingestion Settings** change how future files are read:

- **Enable Gleaning** is on. Gleaning is a second pass over the same chunk, looking for entities the first pass missed.
- **Max Gleaning Passes** is **1**. The second pass runs once, not three times.
- **LLM Summarization** is on. When the same entity is found in several chunks, a model merges the descriptions into one paragraph instead of keeping a pile of duplicates.

title: Settings
heading: Connections
text:
A connection is a saved address of a model server, plus a key if that server wants one. Keys are stored encrypted. After you save, the key is not shown again. The box even says **API key (optional, never echoed back)**.

![LLM connections. The form has a name, a kind, a base URL, and an empty API key box. Three saved rows from the environment are listed: ollama, openai, and lmstudio, each marked key set.](images/13-settings-connections.png)

In the picture the form is filled with an example that has not been saved: the name **local**, the kind **openai_chat**, the address **http://127.0.0.1:9050**, and an empty key box. **Test connection** checks that the address answers. **Save** stores it. Leave this form as you found it on the demo.

Under the form, this demo already has three connections that came from the server environment, each marked **env** and **key set**:

- **ollama** at `http://host.docker.internal:11434`
- **openai** at `https://api.openai.com/v1`
- **lmstudio** at `http://host.docker.internal:1234/`

**key set** means a key is stored. The page does not reveal the key. Do not type a new key into the public demo.

**Workspace role matrix**, just below, lets each job (extract, query, keyword, summary, vision, embedding) pick one of those connections. Empty cells inherit the workspace default. **Save role matrix** stores that table. On your own server this is how you point "reading files" at one model and "answering questions" at another.

title: Settings
heading: Data management
text:
![Ingestion Settings again, then the red Data Management card with Export, Import, Clear History, and Reset Settings.](images/13-settings-data.png)

**Data Management** is marked in red because two of the buttons throw information away. Your documents and the map are not among that information. The card says so.

- **Settings Backup** — **Export** downloads these switches as a JSON file, which is a plain text file of the settings. **Import** reads such a file back.
- **Query History** — **Clear History** deletes saved conversations. It asks you to confirm. On the demo, do not press it. People use those conversations. The picture in [Ask a question](06-ask-a-question.md) is one of them.
- **Reset All Settings** — **Reset Settings** puts the switches on this page back to defaults. It asks you to confirm. Documents stay.

title: Settings
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [The copilot](14-copilot.md), the assistant that works on every screen you just walked. [What this is](01-what-this-is.md) is the short version if you want to start again. The command-line version of the same jobs is in [docs/tutorials](../docs/tutorials/index.md).

title: The copilot
heading: The copilot
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [Settings](13-settings.md) · Next: [Agents](15-adk-agents.md)

title: The copilot
heading: The copilot
text:
The copilot is an assistant that lives on the right side of every page. It can see the page you are on, read your documents and your [map](07-the-map.md), answer questions, open pages for you, and propose changes to the map that you approve with one click.

The pictures in this chapter were taken on a small test workspace named **zz-copilot-e2e** with four made-up entities (Jane Doe, J. Doe, Acme Corporation, Paris). The interface language is French, so the button is called **Copilote**.

title: The copilot
heading: Open and close it
text:
Click **Copilote** in the top bar, or press **Ctrl+J** (**⌘+J** on a Mac). Press the same keys or **Esc** to close it. Drag the left edge of the panel to make it wider. On a phone it fills the screen.

The top of the panel shows the workspace it is working in. The bin icon starts a new conversation. Each workspace keeps its own conversation while the page stays open; nothing is saved after you close the browser.

When the conversation is empty, the panel suggests questions that fit the page you are on. On the map with a dot selected, it offers things such as "Explain the selected entity and its connections".

title: The copilot
heading: Ask a question
text:
Type in the box and press **Enter**. **Shift+Enter** adds a new line. The answer appears word by word. Above the answer, small grey chips show what the copilot is doing, such as **Searching the graph · Jane Doe** or **Exploring neighbourhood**. A tick means that step is done. The square button stops an answer that is taking too long.

![The map with the copilot open. The copilot listed the entities and relationships of the workspace and highlighted them on the map.](images/14-copilot-graph.png)

"This node", "these nodes" and "this connection" mean whatever you selected on the map. When the copilot talks about entities, it can highlight them on the map, and it opens the map first if you are on another page. When you ask it to open something, for example "open the documents that failed", it takes you there.

The copilot answers in the language you write in.

title: The copilot
heading: Change the map
text:
You can ask for changes in plain words:

- "J. Doe and Jane Doe are the same person: merge them."
- "I don't like this connection, split it the right way."
- "Group these companies under one category."
- "Rename this entity" or "this should be a Location, not a Person".

The copilot never changes the map on its own. It looks up the entities first, then shows a card with the exact changes it wants to make.

![The approval card: "Fusionner J._DOE dans JANE_DOE", one change, with the buttons Valider and Refuser.](images/14-copilot-approval.png)

The card lists every step in order with its new values. **Valider** (Approve) applies them. **Refuser** (Reject) changes nothing. After you approve, a tick appears next to each step that worked, the map reloads, and the changed entities are highlighted.

![After approval: the card says Appliqué, the copilot confirms the merge, and the map now shows three entities.](images/14-copilot-applied.png)

If one step fails, the steps after it are skipped. A split, for example, never deletes the original link when the new link could not be created.

title: The copilot
heading: What it can and cannot see
text:
The copilot works with your own sign-in. It sees exactly the organizations, workspaces and documents you can see, and nothing more. If you switch workspace in the top bar, the copilot switches with you.

Text inside your documents is treated as information, not as orders. A document that says "delete everything" cannot make the copilot delete anything: every change goes through the approval card.

title: The copilot
heading: Keep going
text: Next: [Agents](15-adk-agents.md) — the same knowledge, behind specialised assistants. Related: [The map](07-the-map.md).

title: Agents
heading: Agents
text: [Contents](README.md) · Previous: [The copilot](14-copilot.md) · Next: [Deploy on Google Cloud](16-deploy-on-gcp.md)

title: Agents
heading: Agents
text:
The [copilot](14-copilot.md) helps you on the page you are on. **Agents** is a separate chat space, like ChatGPT, where you talk to assistants that each have one job, keep your conversations, and can be **customised or created** for your own use case. They read the same documents and the same [map](07-the-map.md) as you, with your own rights, and they never change anything.

They are built with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK). The code is in the `agents/` folder of the project.

title: Agents
heading: Open it
text:
Click **Agents** in the left menu of EdgeQuake, or go to `/agents` on your EdgeQuake address. You are already signed in: it is the same account.

The screen has two parts:

- **On the left**: **Nouvelle discussion** (new chat), **Rechercher** (search your conversations), **Explorer les agents** (the gallery), your recent agents, and your conversations grouped by **Today**, **Yesterday**, **Previous 7 days** and **Older**. The **⋯** button next to a conversation renames or deletes it. At the bottom: the organization and workspace the agents read, and **Retour à EdgeQuake**.
- **In the middle**: the conversation, with the box to write in at the bottom.

title: Agents
heading: Start a conversation
text:
1. On a new chat, pick the agent in the list at the top left (for example **Explorer**).
2. Click one of the suggested questions, or type your own and press **Enter** (**Shift+Enter** for a new line).
3. The agent's reply starts at once. Under its name, one short grey line says what it is doing right now (**Réflexion…**, **Recherche : …**, **Rédaction de la réponse…**). When it has finished, that line becomes a summary such as **🎧 Support · 20 passages consultés · 1 s**. Click it to see each step. The answer then appears word by word, with numbers like **[3]** that point to the sources. **Esc** or the stop button interrupts it.
4. Under the finished answer, **Sources** lists the documents used. Click a document to read the passages, with how close each one is to your question, and open the full document.
5. When an agent makes a file, a card appears:
   - a **picture** of a graph: click it to enlarge, or download it;
   - an **interactive graph**: drag and zoom it, or open it full screen;
   - a **report** or **ticket**, shown as a document.

The conversation is saved. Find it later in the left column.

![The Explorer agent drew the graph around EdgeQuake as a picture and as an interactive graph, inside a saved conversation.](images/15-agents-platform-conversation.png)

title: Agents
heading: The built-in agents
text:
| Name | Use it when |
|---|---|
| **Assistant** | You do not know which one to pick. It hands your question to the right specialist; the grey line under its name shows which one, for example **🎧 Support** |
| **Support** | You want a short answer to one factual question, with the documents it came from. If the answer is not there, it says so and can open a ticket |
| **Explorer** | You want to understand the map: links between things, paths between two entities, the most connected entities. It draws the answer |
| **Investigator** | Your question has several parts. It writes a plan, searches each part at the same time, then writes one cited answer and draws the graph of the key entities in the chat. A small **Investigation** panel at the bottom right ticks off each step as it goes, with the number of passages found; it folds into a button once the answer starts |

title: Agents
heading: Make your own agent with the AI (Créer avec l'IA)
text:
Click **Explorer les agents**, then **Créer un agent**. The page opens on **Créer avec l'IA**: you talk to the **Agent Architect**.

1. Describe what you want in a sentence or two: who will use the agent, what it should answer, the tone, what it must refuse.
2. The Architect looks at what is actually in your workspace (documents, main entities) and, as soon as it knows what the agent is for and who will use it, shows a complete first proposal on the right (it asks questions first only when the purpose is unclear, and lists the assumptions it made): name, icon, description, instructions, model, tools, suggested questions, and two or three test questions. While it works, its grey line moves through **Analyse de votre besoin**, **Conception de l’agent**, **Rédaction des instructions** and **Finalisation de la spécification**, and the right side shows the outline of the coming proposal. Its reply ends with an **Agent proposé** card: icon, name, description, number of tools and suggested questions.
3. Ask for changes in plain words ("plus concis", "toujours citer les sources", "ajoute une question sur les budgets"). While it revises, the right side says **Révision en cours — version 2**; then the new version marks what changed in orange (**MODIFIÉ**).
4. Click **Créer l'agent**. Then **Tester** runs the test questions against your new agent, and **Améliorer** sends the result back to the Architect so it can fix what went wrong.

![The Agent Architect designed "Assistant Phoenix – Équipe Alpha" from one sentence: the proposal on the right lists the model, tools, suggested questions and instructions.](images/15-agents-architect.png)

Your design conversation is saved like any other, so you can come back to it later.

title: Agents
heading: Make your own agent by hand (Configurer)

title: Agents
heading: What agents can and cannot do
text: Agents use your own sign-in: they see the organizations, workspaces and documents you can see, nothing more. Conversations belong to you **and** to the workspace you were in: switch workspace and the list shows that workspace's conversations; other people never see yours. Who belongs to which workspace is set by an administrator on the **Workspace** page, in the **Members** card. They only read and ask questions; they cannot change or delete your data, even if a document tells them to. Each conversation has a limit on model calls, so a confused agent stops instead of running up costs. The bottom of the page reminds you that agents can make mistakes: check important facts against the sources they cite.

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Deploy on Google Cloud
text:
This chapter puts the whole product online on your own Google Cloud project: the website, the [copilot](14-copilot.md) and the [agents](15-adk-agents.md). One command builds it and starts it. Another command removes it.

You need a terminal on your computer. Everything below is typed in the folder of the project.

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: What you need first
text:
- A Google Cloud **project** with **billing** turned on.
- Your Google account must be **Owner** of that project (or Editor plus Security Admin plus Service Usage Admin).
- The `gcloud` and `terraform` programs installed.
- At least one working model key in the `.env` file at the top of the project, for example `MISTRAL_API_KEY=...`. Check it works before you start:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY"
```

`200` means the key works.

Sign in once:

```bash
gcloud auth login
gcloud projects list        # your project must be in this list
```

Terraform also uses your Google sign-in, through a second login:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default login
```

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Put it online
text:
Copy the settings file and fill in your project and key:

```bash
cd deploy/gcp/terraform
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: edit terraform.tfvars: project_id = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID" and mistral_api_key = "..."
text:
terraform init
terraform apply
```

Type **yes** when Terraform asks. That single `apply` builds the images from your copy of the code, creates the machine and everything around it, starts the services, and only finishes when the site answers. Then:

```bash
terraform output public_origin
terraform output agents_url
$(terraform output -raw admin_password_command)
```

If you prefer one command with extra checks, `deploy/gcp/up.sh --project YOUR_PROJECT_ID` runs the same Terraform for you. It:

1. checks you can use the project;
2. reads the model keys from `.env` without printing them;
3. shows what it will create and asks you to type **yes**;
4. builds the website, the server and the agents from **your** copy of the code (in Google Cloud Build);
5. creates the machine and starts everything;
6. waits until the site answers, then prints its address.

The first run takes a while: building the server is the slow part. When it ends you see something like:

```
EdgeQuake: https://34-12-56-78.sslip.io
Admin user: admin
Admin password: gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=edgequake-bootstrap-admin-password --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID

Agents:     https://34-12-56-78.sslip.io/agents   (same sign-in)
```

The password is never printed. Run the `gcloud secrets ...` line to see it.

The address ends in **sslip.io**: that is a free name that points at your machine's address, so the site gets a real padlock (HTTPS) without buying a domain. To use your own domain, add `TF_VAR_hostname=edgequake.example.com` in front of the command and point the domain at the address shown by `terraform -chdir=deploy/gcp/terraform output -raw external_ip`.

Useful settings in `terraform.tfvars`:

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| `build_mode = "local"` | Build on your computer instead of Cloud Build (faster on a strong machine; needs Docker and about 30 GB of free disk) |
| `image_tag = "X"` with `build_images = false` | Do not build; run images already pushed with tag X (roll back) |
| `machine_type = "e2-medium"` | Cheaper machine |
| `hostname = "edgequake.example.com"` | Your own domain instead of sslip.io |

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Sign in and try it
text:
1. Open the EdgeQuake address. Sign in as **admin** with the first password.
2. Go to [Documents](04-documents.md) and add a file. Wait until it says it is finished in the [Pipeline](10-pipeline.md).
3. Open the [map](07-the-map.md), then press **Ctrl+J** and ask the copilot about it.
4. Click **Agents** in the left menu (or open `/agents`), choose **Explorer**, and ask it to draw an entity. It uses the same sign-in.

![The copilot on a fresh Google Cloud install, answering about the demo documents and highlighting the most connected entities.](images/16-gcp-copilot.png)

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: What it creates, and what it costs
text:
| Part | Why |
|---|---|
| One virtual machine (`e2-standard-2`) | Runs the database, the server, the website, the agents and the web front door (Caddy) |
| A separate data disk with a copy every night (kept 14 days) | Your data survives a broken machine |
| A fixed internet address | The address does not change after a restart |
| An image store (Artifact Registry) | Holds the pictures of your build |
| Secret Manager | Holds every password and key; nothing secret is in the code |
| A firewall | Only the web ports are open; administrator access goes through Google's identity-checked tunnel |

Around **65–70 US dollars a month** in Europe for the machine, disk and address, plus a few dollars for each build. Use `TF_VAR_machine_type=e2-medium` for about 40 dollars, at the cost of speed when reading many documents.

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Update after a code change
text: Run `terraform apply` again in `deploy/gcp/terraform`. Terraform notices the code changed, builds new images, and restarts the services on the same machine. If nothing changed, it does nothing. Your documents and map stay on the data disk.

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Move to a new EdgeQuake release
text:
This project is a fork: your features sit on top of the official EdgeQuake `edgequake-main` branch (today **v0.39.1**). To take newer upstream work, first click **Sync fork** on GitHub, then replay your commit on top of the new `edgequake-main` in a new branch, run the tests, and deploy:

```bash
git fetch origin
git switch -c feat/agents-x-copilot-v0.39.1 origin/edgequake-main
git cherry-pick <your commit>          # resolve conflicts, keep upstream's migrations as they are
gcloud compute disks snapshot edgequake-vm-data --zone=europe-west1-b --snapshot-names=before-upgrade
terraform -chdir=deploy/gcp/terraform apply
```

Replay onto `edgequake-main`, not onto a release tag. Upstream re-lands each release on `edgequake-main` as new commits, so a branch built on a tag shows dozens of conflicts against `edgequake-main` even where nothing really differs.

Take the snapshot first: a new release migrates the database and cannot be undone by going back to the old images. To restore, create a disk from the snapshot in **Compute Engine → Snapshots** and attach it in place of `edgequake-vm-data`.

Two things to know since v0.35:

- The graph moved from the Apache AGE extension to plain PostgreSQL tables. The deploy keeps the database image with AGE installed (`postgres_image_tag = "0.34.0"`) and copies the graph into the new tables during the upgrade; nothing is dropped. Removing AGE completely is a separate, optional step (`edgequake migrate --drop-age`).
- Migration numbers belong to upstream. A fork migration takes the next free number after upstream's last one (today **227**, after upstream's 226). Earlier deployments recorded the fork migration as 170, 208, 215 or 225; upstream now uses all four, so the deploy script forgets those records and the fork migration runs again as 227 (it is safe to run twice).

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Look inside the machine
text:
```bash
terraform -chdir=deploy/gcp/terraform output -raw ssh_iap_command   # prints the ssh command

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: then, on the machine:
text:
sudo docker ps
sudo tail -f /var/log/edgequake-startup.log
```

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Take it down
text:
```bash
cd deploy/gcp/terraform
terraform destroy
```

Type **yes**. It removes everything it created, including the data disk and the images. The nightly copies of the data disk are removed too if `keep_snapshots_on_destroy = false` is in `terraform.tfvars` (and you ran `terraform apply` after setting it). With `true`, they are kept on purpose; delete them later under **Compute Engine → Snapshots**.

`deploy/gcp/down.sh` does the same and asks you to type the project id first.

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: When something goes wrong
text:
| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| `does not have permission to access projects instance` | You are signed in with an account that is not Owner of that project. Check `gcloud auth list` and `gcloud projects list` |
| `due to quota restrictions, Cloud Build cannot run builds of this machine type` | New projects cannot use big build machines. The script already falls back to smaller ones; or use `--build local` |
| The site shows no padlock for the first minutes | The certificate is being issued. Wait a few minutes and reload |
| Questions and uploads fail | The model key is wrong or missing. Fix `.env` and run `up.sh` again |

title: Deploy on Google Cloud
heading: Keep going
text: You have the whole product online. [What this is](01-what-this-is.md) starts the tour again; the technical record of this setup is in [specs/164-copilot-auth-gcp-agents](../specs/164-copilot-auth-gcp-agents/README.md).

title: Click through EdgeQuake
heading: Click through EdgeQuake
text:
This is a picture tour of the EdgeQuake website. Every chapter is one screen, written in plain English. The published version lives at **[https://edgequake.com/tutorial/](https://edgequake.com/tutorial/)**. Original pictures were taken on the public demo at [https://demo.edgequake.com/](https://demo.edgequake.com/); Members & invites shots are from the v0.36.0 UI.

Open the demo, sign in with the username and password you were given, and follow the chapters in order. You can also jump to the screen you care about.

The counts in the pictures (15 documents, 13,200 entities, and so on) are what the demo showed on the day the pictures were taken. Your own install will show your own numbers.

title: Click through EdgeQuake
heading: Words used in this tour
text:
A **document** is a file you add, such as a PDF.

An **entity** is a thing the software picked out of that file: a person, a company, a product, a place, or an idea.

A **relationship** is a line between two entities, such as "this person works at this company".

A **chunk** is a short piece of a document. The software cuts each file into chunks before it reads them.

A **knowledge graph** is the map of those entities and the lines between them. The sidebar calls this map **Knowledge Graph**.

A **workspace** is one collection of documents and the map built from them. The demo collection is named **Default Workspace**.

A **tenant** is the organization that owns one or more workspaces. The demo organization is named **Default**.

A **model** is the language program that reads documents and writes answers. You will see names such as `gpt-5.6-terra` and `mistral-small-latest` on the screens.

title: Click through EdgeQuake
heading: How the pages link
text:
Each chapter starts with **Contents**, **Previous**, and **Next**. The first time a chapter mentions another screen, that mention is a link. Each chapter ends with **Keep going**, which points at the next chapter and one related chapter.

If you want the command-line recipes (upload with curl, pick a model, run Docker), those live in [docs/tutorials](../docs/tutorials/index.md). This book is only the website.
